Do not attempt detector calibration, X-ray tube adjustment, or internal component repair outside approved service procedures. Expected outcome: Unverified image-quality performance is not used for patient diagnosis.

CCR.Complaint: CT staff reported streak artifacts appearing on head studies.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a removable positioning accessory containing a dense external object in the scan field.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the interfering object, inspected the accessory, completed approved image-quality verification, and confirmed the artifact was no longer present.

title: Canon Aquilion ONE / PRISM Edition CT Scanner - Study Will Not Save, Reconstruct, or Export
description: Addresses failed study saving, reconstruction, or export caused by workstation state, storage, workflow, network communication, or software-related conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Data and Avoid Unnecessary Repeat Scans
steps.instructions: Do not repeat a patient scan solely because images are not immediately saving, reconstructing, or exporting. Preserve any available raw data, images, and study identifiers while troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Existing diagnostic data is protected and unnecessary repeat radiation is avoided.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Function Is Failing
steps.instructions: Determine whether the study fails to save locally, reconstruct, display, export to PACS, or complete more than one of these steps. Record any displayed message exactly. Expected outcome: The failed portion of the imaging workflow is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Confirm Workstation Responsiveness
steps.instructions: Verify that the operator workstation is responsive and that the CT application is not frozen or partially unresponsive. Expected outcome: A general workstation problem is identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 4. Verify Study and Patient Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm that the expected patient and study are open and that staff are attempting to save or export the intended examination. Avoid deleting, merging, or modifying patient records during troubleshooting unless required by approved policy. Expected outcome: The problem is not caused by selecting the wrong study or incomplete workflow.

steps.title: 5. Check Local System Status and Storage Indications
steps.instructions: Review normal user-accessible indicators for warnings related to storage, study processing, reconstruction queues, or unavailable resources. Do not manually delete system files or alter storage partitions. Expected outcome: Any visible storage or processing condition is identified without modifying protected system data.

steps.title: 6. Check Network Connectivity for Export Problems
steps.instructions: If local saving and reconstruction work but export fails, inspect accessible network connections and verify whether PACS or other destinations are available. Expected outcome: Local processing and network-transfer problems are separated.

steps.title: 7. Determine Whether the Problem Is Study-Specific
steps.instructions: Check whether another approved test or previously completed study can be accessed or exported without altering patient data. Do not use unrelated patient records unnecessarily. Expected outcome: The issue is narrowed to one study or confirmed to affect general system processing.

steps.title: 8. Perform an Approved Controlled Restart if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If no active reconstruction or data-preservation concern prevents it, and approved procedures allow, perform a controlled workstation or system restart. Do not restart if doing so could jeopardize unsaved or unrecoverable patient data without first escalating. Expected outcome: Processing resumes without data loss and the affected functions return.

steps.title: 9. Verify Complete Study Workflow
steps.instructions: Using an appropriate approved test case, confirm that images can be acquired or accessed, reconstructed, saved, and exported to the intended destination. Confirm receipt at the destination when export is part of the complaint. Expected outcome: The complete study workflow operates normally. If achieved, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Save, Reconstruction, or Export Failure
steps.instructions: If data remains inaccessible, processing repeatedly fails, or study integrity is uncertain, remove the system from clinical use as appropriate and escalate to qualified Canon service and imaging informatics personnel. Do not manipulate databases, reconstruction software, storage arrays, or operating-system files without authorization. Expected outcome: Patient data is preserved and higher-level troubleshooting proceeds without creating additional data risk.

CCR.Complaint: CT staff reported completed studies would reconstruct normally but could not be exported to PACS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found local image processing was normal but the approved network connection to the workstation was disconnected.
CCR.Resolution: Restored the network connection, exported an approved test study, confirmed receipt in PACS, and verified the normal study workflow.

helpfulDetails: Exact save, reconstruction, or export message.

title: Canon Aquilion ONE / PRISM Edition CT Scanner - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Addresses no-power, incomplete startup, or failed initialization caused by power, emergency-stop, workstation, connection, or facility-related conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot the CT system while a patient depends on it for an active or time-critical examination. Remove the patient from the scanner area when necessary and move urgent imaging to another verified system. Confirm whether the reported problem affects the entire CT system, only the operator workstation, or one subsystem. Expected outcome: The patient is safe, an alternate imaging pathway is available, and the exact affected portion of the system is identified. If the system starts normally and remains stable after confirming the reported condition, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Ask clinical staff what occurred immediately before the problem. Determine whether the system is completely unresponsive, partially powered, stuck during initialization, repeatedly restarting, or displaying a specific message. Record any displayed message exactly rather than interpreting it. Expected outcome: The startup failure is reproducible or clearly characterized. If the system now completes startup normally and no abnormal condition remains, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 3. Check Facility and System Power
steps.instructions: Verify that the scanner's normal facility power sources and accessible disconnects or power controls are in their expected operating state. Check for signs of a recent outage, utility interruption, generator transfer, breaker event, or room power problem. Do not reset facility electrical equipment unless authorized by site procedure. Expected outcome: Required power sources are present and no obvious facility power interruption remains. If facility power was the cause and the CT system starts normally after authorized restoration, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Emergency-Stop and Safety Controls
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible emergency-stop controls and other external safety interlocks for an activated, damaged, or abnormal condition. Do not bypass or defeat any interlock. Expected outcome: No emergency-stop or external safety control is preventing normal startup. If an activated control is safely restored according to approved procedure and startup completes normally, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect External Connections and Workstation Power
steps.instructions: Check accessible power cords, workstation power connections, display connections, and external communication cables for looseness, damage, or accidental disconnection. Reseat only user-accessible or service-approved connections. Expected outcome: External connections are secure and undamaged. If restoring an external connection resolves startup, complete functional verification and stop.

steps.title: 6. Verify Operator Workstation and Display Operation
steps.instructions: Determine whether the workstation, monitors, keyboard, mouse, and other operator-interface components are powered and responsive. A blank display can be mistaken for a scanner startup failure. Expected outcome: The operator interface powers normally and accepts input. If the scanner was operating but the workstation or display connection was the only problem, correct the external cause and verify normal control.

steps.title: 7. Check Room and Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Look for excessive heat, blocked equipment-room ventilation, water intrusion, unusual odor, smoke, or evidence of a cooling problem. Do not continue powering equipment that shows evidence of overheating, electrical damage, water exposure, or burning odor. Expected outcome: Environmental conditions are suitable for continued evaluation. If an unsafe environmental condition is present, remove the equipment from service and escalate immediately.

steps.title: 8. Perform an Approved Controlled Restart if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the system is stable, no patient is dependent on it, and site/manufacturer procedures permit it, perform a normal controlled shutdown and restart using approved operating controls. Do not repeatedly cycle system power in response to recurring failures. Expected outcome: The CT system completes its normal startup sequence without recurring faults. If startup completes and remains stable, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm that the operator workstation is responsive, required scanner subsystems indicate ready status, gantry and table controls are available, and no unresolved startup or safety messages remain. Use approved operational checks before returning the scanner to clinical use. Expected outcome: The CT system starts normally and reaches a stable ready condition. If achieved, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If the system still will not start or initialize, stop external troubleshooting. Do not proceed into power distribution assemblies, cabinets, internal electronics, or restricted service functions without appropriate authorization and documentation. Expected outcome: An unresolved system is kept out of clinical service and routed for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: CT staff reported the Aquilion ONE / PRISM Edition would not complete startup after a facility power interruption.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found facility power had been restored but an accessible system power connection had not returned to its normal operating condition.
CCR.Resolution: Restored the approved external power condition, confirmed successful system startup and ready status, and verified normal operator controls before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the entire system or only the workstation was affected.
Recent power outage or generator transfer.
Evidence of heat, odor, water, or damage.

title: Canon Aquilion ONE / PRISM Edition CT Scanner - Workstation Freezes or Loses Communication
description: Addresses workstation freezes or communication loss caused by power, cables, network connections, peripheral problems, software state, or infrastructure interruptions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Examination Data
steps.instructions: Do not continue scanning when the operator workstation is unreliable or communication with the scanner is lost. If a patient is on the table, safely conclude or terminate the examination according to approved clinical procedures and use alternate imaging if needed. Expected outcome: The patient is protected and unnecessary data loss is minimized.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the workstation is completely frozen, only one application is unresponsive, communication with the gantry is lost, or the display/input devices are not responding. Record displayed messages exactly. Expected outcome: The problem is clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Check Workstation Power and Peripherals
steps.instructions: Verify workstation power, monitor status, keyboard, mouse, and other accessible peripherals. Inspect external power and data connections for looseness or damage. Expected outcome: A peripheral or simple power issue is either corrected or ruled out.

steps.title: 4. Check Scanner-to-Workstation Connectivity
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible network and system communication cables between approved external connection points. Do not disconnect internal scanner communication wiring. Expected outcome: External communication connections are secure. If reseating an approved external connection restores stable communication, continue to functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Determine Whether the Problem Is Local or Network-Wide
steps.instructions: Ask whether other networked systems are experiencing communication problems and whether the CT scanner remains responsive locally. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to the CT workstation or a broader infrastructure issue.

steps.title: 6. Check for Recent Power or Network Events
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem followed an outage, network change, switch maintenance, software update, or system restart. Expected outcome: Relevant recent events are identified.

steps.title: 7. Perform an Approved Controlled Workstation Restart
steps.instructions: If no active patient procedure depends on the workstation and approved procedures permit it, perform a normal controlled restart. Avoid repeated hard power-offs unless required by authorized service procedures. Expected outcome: The workstation restarts and re-establishes stable communication.

steps.title: 8. Verify Scanner and Application Communication
steps.instructions: Confirm that the workstation communicates with the scanner, expected system statuses populate normally, and required control functions are available. Expected outcome: Communication remains stable without recurring freezes.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Use an approved non-patient workflow to verify workstation responsiveness, scanner communication, study handling, and data availability. Expected outcome: The workstation remains responsive and required CT communication functions normally. If achieved, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Recurrent Freeze or Communication Loss
steps.instructions: If freezing or communication loss returns, remove the scanner from service as appropriate. Do not modify restricted software, internal network configuration, operating-system files, or service applications without authorization. Expected outcome: An unreliable workstation is escalated before clinical use resumes.

CCR.Complaint: CT staff reported the operator workstation froze and lost communication with the scanner.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an accessible workstation network connection was loose.
CCR.Resolution: Secured the connection, restarted the workstation using the approved process, and verified stable scanner communication and normal non-patient workflow.

helpfulDetails: Whether the entire workstation or one application froze.

title: Canon Vantage Orian MRI System - Calibration or Quality-Control Test Fails
description: Addresses failed MRI calibration or QC checks caused by setup, phantom positioning, coils, environmental conditions, system readiness, or repeatable performance problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Use
steps.instructions: If a required quality-control or calibration check has failed and scanner performance cannot be confirmed, do not assume the system is suitable for continued clinical scanning. Follow facility policy regarding removal or restriction from clinical use. Expected outcome: Patient imaging is not performed on a scanner whose required performance verification is unresolved.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Failed Test
steps.instructions: Document the specific QC or calibration process that failed and capture the exact displayed message or reported result. Do not substitute an interpretation for the actual failure description. Expected outcome: The failed process and observed result are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify System Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm the scanner has completed startup, no unrelated system fault is active, and the MRI has reached its normal ready condition before the test is repeated. Expected outcome: The QC failure is not simply the result of incomplete system initialization.

steps.title: 4. Check the Test Object or Phantom
steps.instructions: Inspect the approved phantom or test device for damage, leakage, contamination, incorrect assembly, or other obvious condition that could invalidate the test. Expected outcome: The test object is appropriate and suitable for use.

steps.title: 5. Verify Phantom Positioning
steps.instructions: Confirm that the phantom is positioned and aligned according to the approved QC procedure and that the table and selected coil are set up correctly. Do not invent alternate positioning to force a passing result. Expected outcome: Test setup matches the approved procedure.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Coil and External Connections
steps.instructions: Verify the required coil and accessible connections are secure and physically intact. If allowed by the approved test procedure, compare with another known-good compatible accessory when an accessory fault is suspected. Expected outcome: No external coil or connection issue invalidates the test.

steps.title: 7. Check Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Determine whether the failed test followed a room temperature problem, HVAC event, power interruption, facility work, equipment relocation, or other environmental change. Expected outcome: No obvious external environmental condition explains the failure.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Approved Test Once Conditions Are Correct
steps.instructions: After correcting any external setup issue, repeat the same approved QC or calibration procedure without altering acceptance criteria. Expected outcome: The test completes normally and meets the established manufacturer or facility criteria. If the test passes and no other abnormal condition is present, troubleshooting can stop after documentation.

steps.title: 9. Do Not Adjust Calibration to Chase a Passing Result
steps.instructions: If the approved test continues to fail, do not change internal calibration, shim, RF, gradient, or restricted service parameters without the required qualification and manufacturer procedure. Expected outcome: The failed test remains an accurate indication of system condition rather than being masked by unauthorized adjustment.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent QC Failure
steps.instructions: Remove the scanner from service or restrict clinical use according to policy and arrange qualified service evaluation. Expected outcome: Persistent performance failures receive appropriate service-level investigation.

CCR.Complaint: MRI staff reported the scheduled image-quality QC test would not pass.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the QC phantom was incorrectly positioned in the selected coil.
CCR.Resolution: Repositioned the phantom according to the approved QC setup, repeated the test successfully, and documented the passing result before return to service.

title: Canon Vantage Orian MRI System - Cooling, Fan, or Overtemperature Fault Occurs
description: Addresses cooling warnings, abnormal fan conditions, or temperature faults caused by airflow obstruction, room conditions, facility HVAC, or service-level cooling problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Unreliable Operation
steps.instructions: If the system reports an overtemperature condition, shuts down, or cooling reliability is uncertain, stop clinical scanning and remove the patient using the normal MRI-safe workflow. Do not continue scanning to determine whether the fault worsens. Expected outcome: No patient depends on equipment with a possible thermal-control problem.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Condition
steps.instructions: Document the displayed warning or fault exactly. Ask whether staff noticed unusual fan noise, reduced airflow, heat, odor, repeated shutdowns, or a room-temperature problem. Expected outcome: The thermal complaint and associated symptoms are clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Scanner Environment
steps.instructions: Check the equipment room and scan room for unusual temperature, blocked ventilation areas, nearby construction, closed vents, portable equipment obstructing airflow, or other obvious environmental changes. Expected outcome: Required external airflow paths appear unobstructed and the environment is not obviously abnormal.

steps.title: 4. Check Facility HVAC Status
steps.instructions: Determine whether the facility HVAC system is operating normally and whether there has been a recent alarm, maintenance event, power interruption, or loss of environmental control. Do not attempt to compensate for a facility HVAC failure by repeatedly restarting the MRI. Expected outcome: Facility environmental support is confirmed or the appropriate Facilities team is engaged.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Airflow Areas
steps.instructions: Without removing protected panels, inspect accessible intake and exhaust areas for obvious blockage, debris, or items stored too close to ventilation paths. Expected outcome: Accessible airflow areas are clear.

steps.title: 6. Listen for Abnormal Cooling Sounds
steps.instructions: From a safe location, note whether expected cooling fans appear to operate or whether there is unusual grinding, rattling, cycling, or silence associated with the complaint. Do not open cabinets to inspect internal fans. Expected outcome: No obvious external evidence of a mechanical cooling problem is present.

steps.title: 7. Allow Recovery Only According to Approved Procedures
steps.instructions: If the issue was caused by a verified room-environment problem and approved procedures permit recovery after conditions normalize, allow the system to return to its normal state without repeated forced restarts. Expected outcome: The system returns to a normal ready condition without recurring thermal warning.

steps.title: 8. Verify Stability Before Clinical Use
steps.instructions: Observe the scanner through an appropriate functional check after the identified external cause is corrected. Verify no cooling or temperature warning returns and the system remains stable. Expected outcome: Normal system readiness is maintained without abnormal heat or cooling indications. If achieved, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Stop for Heat, Odor, Smoke, or Recurring Thermal Faults
steps.instructions: If abnormal heat, burning odor, smoke, repeated overtemperature warnings, or unusual internal noise is present, stop troubleshooting immediately. Do not energize the system repeatedly. Expected outcome: A potentially unsafe thermal condition is isolated from clinical use.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Cooling Problems
steps.instructions: If environmental and airflow checks are normal but the warning remains or returns, remove the MRI from service for qualified evaluation. Expected outcome: Internal cooling or thermal-control problems are handled at the appropriate service level.

CCR.Complaint: MRI staff reported a temperature warning and scanner shutdown during operation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the equipment-room HVAC was not maintaining normal environmental conditions.
CCR.Resolution: Coordinated HVAC correction with Facilities, verified the room condition normalized, and confirmed the MRI returned to stable operation without recurrence during functional verification.

helpfulDetails: Room condition at time of fault
Fan noise or lack of airflow

title: Canon Vantage Orian MRI System - Detector or Acquisition Hardware Is Not Ready
description: Addresses acquisition-not-ready conditions involving coils, connections, scanner readiness, accessories, configuration, or other externally verifiable acquisition-path problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Clinical Acquisition
steps.instructions: If acquisition hardware is unreliable, do not continue scanning a patient in an attempt to determine whether the problem clears. End the affected workflow safely and move the patient to another verified imaging option if necessary. Expected outcome: No patient depends on unreliable acquisition hardware.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine what staff mean by “not ready.” Record any displayed message exactly and identify whether the problem occurs with every exam, one coil, one patient setup, or one specific protocol. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to the overall scanner or a particular acquisition setup.

steps.title: 3. Verify General Scanner Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm the Canon Vantage Orian has completed startup and is otherwise in its normal ready state. Check for unrelated system warnings that may prevent acquisition hardware from becoming available. Expected outcome: No broader startup or system-readiness condition explains the complaint.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Selected MRI Coil
steps.instructions: Inspect the coil being used for visible damage, damaged housing, contamination, unusual wear, or compromised cable condition. Do not use a visibly damaged MRI coil clinically. Expected outcome: The coil is physically intact and appropriate for evaluation. If damage is present, remove that accessory from service and retest the scanner using an approved known-good compatible coil when appropriate.

steps.title: 5. Verify Coil and Accessory Connections
steps.instructions: Check that accessible coil connectors and other examination accessories are fully seated, properly positioned, and free of obvious damage or contamination. Do not force connectors or manipulate internal contacts. Expected outcome: All accessible acquisition-related connections are secure. If reseating an approved external connection restores normal readiness, proceed to verification.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Known-Good Compatible Coil
steps.instructions: When appropriate, substitute another approved compatible coil or accessory known to work on the system. This helps separate a scanner-level problem from an accessory-specific problem. Expected outcome: The result identifies whether the issue follows the original coil/accessory or remains with the scanner. If the problem follows one coil, remove that coil from service and document the finding.

steps.title: 7. Verify Exam Setup and Coil Selection
steps.instructions: Review normal operator-visible exam setup to make sure the intended coil, patient orientation, exam selection, and other routine settings are appropriate. Do not alter restricted configuration or calibration values. Expected outcome: The examination configuration matches the connected hardware and intended workflow.

steps.title: 8. Inspect the Scan Environment
steps.instructions: Verify no obvious loose accessory, misplaced cable, recently added equipment, or environmental change is interfering with the normal acquisition setup. Expected outcome: The external scan environment is suitable and no obvious setup problem remains.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Controlled Functional Check
steps.instructions: With a known-good external setup, verify that the acquisition hardware reaches the expected ready state and that an approved test workflow can proceed as appropriate. Expected outcome: The system recognizes required acquisition hardware and becomes ready without recurring warnings. If achieved, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Acquisition-Readiness Failures
steps.instructions: If multiple known-good coils or setups fail, acquisition hardware remains unavailable, or the system repeatedly drops readiness, stop external troubleshooting. Do not access RF cabinets, receiver electronics, gradient hardware, internal cabling, or restricted service functions. Expected outcome: The system is removed from clinical service for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: MRI staff reported the Canon Vantage Orian would not indicate acquisition readiness with the selected imaging coil.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the condition followed one specific coil while a known-good compatible coil was recognized normally.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the affected coil from service, verified normal scanner readiness with the known-good coil, and returned the MRI system to service after functional verification.

title: Canon Vantage Orian MRI System - DICOM, PACS, or Worklist Transfer Fails
description: Addresses failed worklist retrieval or image transfer caused by network connectivity, destination availability, configuration, patient data, or interface conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Workflow and Patient Data
steps.instructions: A network transfer problem does not automatically mean the scanner itself is unsafe, but do not allow studies to be lost or unidentified. Maintain a verified method to preserve patient and study information while troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient data remains protected and clinical workflow has an appropriate contingency.

steps.title: 2. Identify Which Function Has Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue involves modality worklist retrieval, DICOM send, PACS receipt, query/retrieve, or another interface. Confirm whether the failure affects all studies or only one patient or destination. Expected outcome: The affected communication path is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Confirm the MRI Workstation Is Otherwise Functional
steps.instructions: Verify the scanner and workstation are operating normally and that completed study data is present locally when appropriate. Expected outcome: The issue is isolated to data communication rather than a general scanner failure.

steps.title: 4. Check Physical Network Connectivity
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible Ethernet or interface connections for secure seating and visible damage. Observe normal connection indicators if they are available without entering restricted service areas. Expected outcome: The physical network connection appears intact.

steps.title: 5. Determine Whether Other Systems Are Affected
steps.instructions: Ask whether other imaging modalities, workstations, or hospital systems can access PACS or the worklist. A broader outage should be escalated to the appropriate IT/PACS team rather than treated as an MRI hardware failure. Expected outcome: The problem is categorized as MRI-specific or infrastructure-wide.

steps.title: 6. Verify the Intended Destination or Service Is Available
steps.instructions: Using approved operator-visible functions, confirm that the expected destination or worklist service is selected and available. Do not change network addresses, ports, application entities, or protected interface configuration without authorization and verified reference information. Expected outcome: The scanner is attempting to communicate with the intended configured destination.

steps.title: 7. Check Patient and Study Information
steps.instructions: For a failure affecting only one study, verify that required patient and exam information appears complete and consistent in the normal clinical workflow. Do not alter identifiers merely to force a transfer. Expected outcome: No obvious data-entry or study-selection problem explains the failure.

steps.title: 8. Retry the Transfer Through the Approved Workflow
steps.instructions: After confirming network and destination availability, retry the failed transfer or worklist query using the normal approved interface. Expected outcome: Communication completes successfully without recurring error. If successful, verify receipt at the destination before closing the issue.

steps.title: 9. Confirm End-to-End Receipt
steps.instructions: Coordinate with PACS, radiology, or IT staff as needed to confirm that the expected study actually arrived and is associated correctly. A local “sent” status alone may not prove successful end-to-end delivery. Expected outcome: The complete MRI-to-destination communication path is verified. If achieved, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Communication Failure
steps.instructions: If physical connectivity is normal but transfers or worklist communication continue to fail, involve the appropriate PACS, network, integration, or Canon service support group. Expected outcome: Configuration or infrastructure problems are escalated without unauthorized changes.

CCR.Complaint: MRI staff reported completed studies from the Canon Vantage Orian were not reaching PACS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the scanner's accessible network connection had become disconnected.
CCR.Resolution: Restored the network connection, resent the affected study through the approved workflow, and confirmed successful receipt in PACS.

helpfulDetails: Function affected: worklist, send, query, or retrieve

title: Canon Vantage Orian MRI System - Exposure or Scan Will Not Start or Is Aborted
description: Addresses MRI scan sequences that will not begin or terminate unexpectedly because of readiness, setup, coil, patient, communication, or environmental conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Repeated Scan Attempts
steps.instructions: If a scan repeatedly fails or aborts, do not continue retrying while a patient depends on unreliable operation. Assess the clinical situation and transfer the patient to another verified imaging workflow when necessary. Expected outcome: Patient care is maintained without relying on an unstable scanner.

steps.title: 2. Confirm How the Scan Fails
steps.instructions: Determine whether the scan never begins, starts and immediately aborts, stops partway through acquisition, or fails only with one exam or protocol. Record displayed messages exactly and note when during the workflow the failure occurs. Expected outcome: The failure point is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Overall System Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm startup is complete, the scanner is not reporting another unresolved fault, and required subsystems indicate normal readiness. Expected outcome: No general system condition prevents scanning.

steps.title: 4. Check Patient and Table Positioning
steps.instructions: Verify the table is properly positioned, patient setup is complete, and no positioning issue, cable routing problem, or accessory obstruction is preventing the scan workflow. Expected outcome: Patient positioning and table status are appropriate for the examination.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Coil and Connections
steps.instructions: Confirm the required imaging coil is correctly connected and physically intact. Check accessible connectors and cables for incomplete seating or visible damage. Expected outcome: Required acquisition accessories are recognized and secure. If correcting the coil connection restores scan operation, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Routine Exam Settings
steps.instructions: Review operator-visible patient orientation, exam selection, coil selection, and other routine settings involved in the attempted scan. Do not alter protected service configuration or calibration values. Expected outcome: The scan setup matches the intended examination and connected hardware.

steps.title: 7. Determine Whether the Failure Is Protocol-Specific
steps.instructions: When clinically appropriate and without a patient dependent on the scanner, compare operation using another approved routine workflow or test setup. Do not modify clinical protocols solely to bypass a persistent fault. Expected outcome: The problem is identified as either specific to one workflow or present across scanning generally.

steps.title: 8. Check for Recent Environmental or Infrastructure Changes
steps.instructions: Ask whether the problem followed a power event, HVAC issue, network interruption, software event, facility maintenance activity, or equipment change in or near the MRI environment. Expected outcome: External environmental or infrastructure causes are either identified or reasonably excluded.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Controlled Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting any external cause, verify the system can initiate and complete an appropriate approved scan/test acquisition without aborting or displaying the original condition. Expected outcome: The scan begins, proceeds, and completes normally with stable system readiness. If achieved, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Repeated Scan Abortions
steps.instructions: If scans continue to abort with known-good accessories and correct setup, remove the MRI from clinical service. Do not investigate internal RF, gradient, power, control, or magnet-related hardware beyond authorized external checks. Expected outcome: The scanner is referred for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: MRI staff reported scans would not start and the system returned to a not-ready condition.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the selected imaging coil connection was not fully seated.
CCR.Resolution: Secured the coil connection, confirmed normal hardware recognition, and completed an approved functional scan without recurrence.

helpfulDetails: Whether scan failed before or during acquisition

title: Canon Vantage Orian MRI System - Gantry, Table, or Positioning Motion Is Unavailable
description: Addresses unavailable patient-table or positioning movement caused by controls, obstructions, emergency states, accessories, positioning, or system readiness conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Before Testing Motion
steps.instructions: If a patient is on the table and motion is unreliable, stop nonessential movement and follow the approved patient-removal workflow. Do not continue troubleshooting motion while a patient depends on the system. Maintain MRI-compatible equipment and Zone IV controls throughout the response. Expected outcome: The patient is safe and table motion can be evaluated without clinical dependency.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Motion Is Unavailable
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves longitudinal table travel, table height, positioning controls, a specific control location, or all patient-positioning movement. Ask whether the problem is constant or occurs only at a particular table position. Expected outcome: The affected movement and control location are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Physical Obstruction
steps.instructions: Visually inspect around the patient table, bore entrance, floor path, cables, pads, straps, coils, positioning aids, and nearby equipment. Remove only items that can be safely repositioned without disturbing scanner hardware. Expected outcome: The table path and positioning area are clear of external obstructions. If an obstruction was preventing motion and normal movement returns after removal, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Emergency and Safety Controls
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible emergency-stop or motion-stop controls and verify that no obvious safety control has been activated. Do not bypass a stop circuit or defeat an interlock. Expected outcome: No externally activated safety control is preventing movement.

steps.title: 5. Verify Scanner Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm that the MRI has completed startup and is not displaying a general system-not-ready condition. Positioning motion may be intentionally unavailable when another subsystem is faulted or initialization is incomplete. Expected outcome: The scanner is otherwise in a normal state that should permit positioning. If the system itself is not ready, troubleshoot the broader readiness problem instead of forcing table movement.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Accessible Table Controls
steps.instructions: Test only approved user-accessible table controls with the table unloaded when practical. Compare operation from available control locations if the system provides more than one approved control point. Look for damaged buttons, stuck controls, contamination, or obvious physical damage. Expected outcome: Controls respond normally or the issue is isolated to a specific external control interface. If one accessible control works and another does not, remove the scanner from clinical use until the defective positioning control is evaluated if that control is required for safe operation.

steps.title: 7. Check Accessories and Patient-Positioning Items
steps.instructions: Verify that coils, pads, supports, straps, cables, and other accessories are installed and routed so they do not interfere with table travel or create tension during movement. Expected outcome: No accessory or cable routing problem restricts table motion.

steps.title: 8. Test Motion Through a Safe Limited Range
steps.instructions: With no patient dependent on the equipment, test the affected positioning function through an appropriate safe range using normal controls. Stop immediately for binding, grinding, unexpected movement, hesitation, or abnormal sound. Expected outcome: Table or positioning movement is smooth, controlled, repeatable, and stops normally when commanded. If normal motion is restored and repeatable, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify all clinically required positioning controls involved in the complaint operate normally. Confirm there is no unexpected motion, obstruction, persistent message, or control failure. Expected outcome: The table can be positioned reliably using normal controls and the scanner remains ready for use. If achieved, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Motion Problems
steps.instructions: If the table will not move, moves unpredictably, binds, generates unusual noise, or repeatedly becomes unavailable without an external cause, stop testing. Do not access internal drive assemblies, motor controls, or restricted service functions. Expected outcome: The scanner is removed from service for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: MRI staff reported the patient table would not advance into the scanner bore.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a positioning accessory and cable were interfering with the table travel path.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the accessory and cable routing, verified smooth table travel with normal controls, and confirmed the scanner remained clinically ready.

title: Canon Vantage Orian MRI System - Image Quality Is Poor or Artifacts Are Present
description: Addresses degraded MRI images and artifacts caused by positioning, motion, coils, accessories, external interference, setup, or environmental conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Confirm Clinical Usability
steps.instructions: If images are unreliable for diagnosis, do not continue using the scanner as though image quality is acceptable. Coordinate an alternate imaging pathway if necessary. Expected outcome: Clinical decisions are not based on known unreliable images.

steps.title: 2. Characterize the Image Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves noise, shading, signal loss, ghosting, distortion, banding, unusual bright or dark areas, or another visible artifact. Determine whether it affects every study, one coil, one exam type, or one patient. Expected outcome: The artifact pattern and affected workflows are clearly identified without prematurely assigning a cause.

steps.title: 3. Verify Patient Positioning and Motion Factors
steps.instructions: Review patient positioning, immobilization, comfort, and the likelihood of voluntary or involuntary movement during the examination. Expected outcome: Positioning is appropriate and obvious motion-related causes are corrected when possible. If image quality becomes normal after correcting patient positioning or motion, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Coil and Coil Placement
steps.instructions: Check the selected MRI coil for visible damage and confirm it is positioned correctly for the intended anatomy. Verify coil elements, cables, and accessories are not compressed, sharply bent, trapped, or improperly arranged. Expected outcome: The coil is intact, correctly positioned, and properly connected.

steps.title: 5. Compare With a Known-Good Coil or Setup
steps.instructions: When appropriate, repeat an approved test using another compatible known-good coil or established test setup. Expected outcome: The comparison shows whether the image-quality problem follows a specific coil/accessory or remains with the scanner. If the problem follows one coil, remove that coil from service.

steps.title: 6. Check External Items in the Scan Environment
steps.instructions: Look for newly introduced equipment, cables, accessories, powered devices, or other changes in or near the MRI environment that could contribute to interference or image degradation. Follow MRI safety rules when removing or relocating equipment. Expected outcome: No obvious external interference source remains.

steps.title: 7. Verify Routine Scan Setup
steps.instructions: Check operator-visible protocol selection, coil selection, patient orientation, field positioning, and other routine exam parameters for accidental mismatch. Do not alter restricted calibration or service settings. Expected outcome: The examination is configured correctly for the intended acquisition.

steps.title: 8. Determine Whether the Problem Is Reproducible
steps.instructions: Using an approved quality-control phantom or established test process when available, determine whether the reported artifact can be reproduced independent of the original patient. Expected outcome: The problem is identified as patient/setup-specific or scanner/accessory-related.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Image-Quality Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting an external cause, verify that an approved test or quality-control acquisition produces expected image quality without the reported artifact. Expected outcome: Image quality is restored and the original artifact is no longer present. If achieved, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Image-Quality Problems
steps.instructions: If the artifact remains across known-good coils, appropriate test setups, and multiple approved acquisitions, remove the scanner from service or restrict use according to facility policy until qualified evaluation is completed. Do not adjust internal RF, gradient, shim, magnet, or calibration parameters outside authorized procedures. Expected outcome: Persistent quality problems are escalated without unauthorized internal adjustment.

CCR.Complaint: MRI staff reported localized signal loss on examinations performed with one imaging coil.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering reproduced the problem with that coil and obtained normal images using a known-good compatible coil.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the affected coil from service and verified acceptable image quality with the known-good coil using the approved test workflow.

title: Canon Vantage Orian MRI System - Study Will Not Save, Reconstruct, or Export
description: Addresses studies that cannot be saved, reconstructed, or exported because of workflow, storage, software, communication, destination, or data-related conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Data Before Taking Action
steps.instructions: Do not restart or power-cycle the workstation until the status of unsaved or unreconstructed patient data has been considered. Preserve available study information whenever possible. If clinical workflow cannot continue reliably, move future imaging to another verified system. Expected outcome: Existing patient data is protected as much as possible and no new studies are placed at unnecessary risk.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Failed Function
steps.instructions: Determine whether the study failed to save locally, failed during reconstruction, cannot be opened, or cannot be exported to the intended destination. Determine whether the problem affects all studies or only one examination. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to local storage, reconstruction, or export.

steps.title: 3. Verify Workstation Responsiveness
steps.instructions: Confirm the workstation is responsive and not frozen or displaying broader system errors. Expected outcome: The issue is distinguished from a general workstation failure.

steps.title: 4. Confirm the Study Is Present
steps.instructions: Using normal operator-visible functions, determine whether the acquired images or raw study information expected from the workflow are still visible locally. Do not delete studies or temporary data as a troubleshooting shortcut. Expected outcome: The availability of the affected study data is known.

steps.title: 5. Check for Obvious Storage or Queue Conditions
steps.instructions: Review normal operator-visible storage or transfer status indicators for a full queue, pending job, or storage warning. Do not manually delete patient studies unless authorized under the facility's data-retention and recovery procedures. Expected outcome: Any visible storage or queue condition is identified without risking patient data.

steps.title: 6. Determine Whether the Failure Is Study-Specific
steps.instructions: Check whether another previously completed or approved test study can be accessed or processed normally without creating unnecessary patient data. Expected outcome: The problem is identified as isolated to one study or affecting the system generally.

steps.title: 7. Check Export Destination Availability
steps.instructions: If local saving and reconstruction work but export fails, verify the intended PACS or other approved destination is available and that network connectivity appears normal. Expected outcome: Export failure is separated from local reconstruction or storage failure.

steps.title: 8. Retry Only Through the Normal Approved Workflow
steps.instructions: After correcting any obvious external condition, retry the save, reconstruction, or export action using the standard workflow. Avoid repeated retries if the system continues returning the same failure. Expected outcome: The process completes successfully without duplicating or corrupting workflow data.

steps.title: 9. Verify the Final Data Path
steps.instructions: Confirm the study can be opened locally when applicable, reconstructed images are complete, and exported data is received at the intended destination. Expected outcome: Study integrity and the complete clinical data path are verified. If achieved, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Data or Reconstruction Failures
steps.instructions: If studies repeatedly fail to save or reconstruct, data disappears, the workstation reports storage problems, or multiple studies are affected, stop clinical use and escalate. Do not manipulate databases, operating-system files, reconstruction services, or internal storage outside approved service procedures. Expected outcome: Patient data and system integrity are protected while qualified support investigates the failure.

CCR.Complaint: MRI staff reported completed studies were reconstructing normally but would not export to PACS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the workstation had lost its external network connection while local study storage remained functional.
CCR.Resolution: Restored the network connection, resent the affected study, confirmed receipt in PACS, and verified normal subsequent export operation.

helpfulDetails: Save, reconstruct, or export function affected
Final local and PACS study status

title: Canon Vantage Orian MRI System - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Addresses no-power, incomplete startup, startup hangs, and readiness failures caused by external power, shutdown state, controls, connections, or environmental conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Clinical Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable MRI system while a patient depends on it. Remove any patient from the scanner using the established MRI-safe workflow and provide an alternate imaging plan if needed. Observe all MRI Zone IV safety requirements during troubleshooting. Expected outcome: No patient is dependent on the affected system, and the scanner can be evaluated safely. If patient safety and workflow have been secured, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Condition
steps.instructions: Ask staff what occurred when the system was last operating normally and what happened during the failed startup. Determine whether the system is completely unpowered, powers partially, stops during initialization, displays a message, or leaves only one subsystem unavailable. Record any displayed message exactly rather than interpreting it. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to no power, partial power, or an incomplete startup sequence. If the system subsequently completes startup normally and remains stable, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 3. Check Facility Power and External Power Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify that the scanner area has normal facility power and that no obvious building power interruption, tripped upstream disconnect, emergency power event, or facilities-related shutdown is present. Do not reset breakers, disconnects, or emergency controls unless authorized by facility procedure and manufacturer documentation. Expected outcome: Required facility power appears available and no external power interruption explains the condition. If facility power is abnormal, stop troubleshooting and involve Facilities or the appropriate electrical support group.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Power and Control Interfaces
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible operator controls, power indicators, emergency-stop controls, and external cabinets for signs of an unintended shutdown condition, loose accessible connection, physical damage, unusual odor, heat, or liquid exposure. Do not open energized cabinets or bypass safety interlocks. Expected outcome: External controls are in their normal operating condition with no obvious damage or unsafe condition. If physical damage, burning odor, abnormal heat, or liquid intrusion is present, remove the system from service and escalate.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Startup Sequence Is Being Performed From the Correct State
steps.instructions: Confirm that the scanner was not left in an unusual shutdown, service, emergency, or facility-isolated state. Use only approved normal operator startup controls and documented procedures. Do not repeatedly power-cycle the MRI system in an attempt to force startup. Expected outcome: The scanner receives one controlled startup attempt from a known normal state. If startup completes and all required subsystems report ready, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 6. Check Connected Operator Equipment
steps.instructions: Verify the operator workstation, monitors, keyboard, mouse, network-connected consoles, and other externally accessible components have power and secure connections. A powered scanner with an unavailable workstation can be mistaken for a scanner startup failure. Expected outcome: Operator equipment is powered, connected, and responsive. If correcting an external connection restores normal system initialization, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 7. Consider Recent Environmental or Infrastructure Events
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue followed a power outage, utility work, HVAC problem, network outage, maintenance activity, water event, or other infrastructure change. MRI systems depend on multiple facility services, and startup may remain incomplete when a supporting service is unavailable. Expected outcome: No unresolved infrastructure condition is identified, or the responsible support group has been engaged.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After any external cause is corrected, allow the system to complete its normal startup and readiness checks. Verify the operator workstation is responsive, the scanner reaches its normal ready condition, and no abnormal warning remains. Do not return the system to clinical use merely because power has been restored. Expected outcome: The Canon Vantage Orian completes startup normally, remains stable, and reaches the expected clinical ready state. If achieved, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 9. Escalate an Unresolved Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If power is present but startup repeatedly stops, a subsystem remains unavailable, or unexplained warnings persist, do not proceed into internal cabinets or restricted service functions. Expected outcome: The unresolved system is removed from clinical service and referred for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: MRI staff reported the Canon Vantage Orian would power partially but would not complete normal startup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an externally powered operator component was not receiving power following a facility interruption.
CCR.Resolution: Restored the external power condition, confirmed normal system startup and workstation operation, and verified the scanner reached its clinical ready state.

helpfulDetails: Exact startup message or screen condition
Any unusual heat, odor, sound, or damage

title: Canon Vantage Orian MRI System - Workstation Freezes or Loses Communication
description: Addresses frozen operator workstations, unresponsive controls, and communication loss caused by power, connections, network conditions, software state, or peripheral problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Dependence on the Frozen Workstation
steps.instructions: If the workstation becomes unresponsive during an examination, do not continue clinical scanning through an unreliable control path. Follow the approved workflow to protect and remove the patient if needed. Expected outcome: No patient depends on an unstable workstation or communication path.

steps.title: 2. Define What Is Actually Frozen
steps.instructions: Determine whether the mouse and keyboard are unresponsive, one application has stopped responding, the entire workstation is frozen, the scanner is disconnected from the workstation, or another system such as PACS is unavailable. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to the workstation, scanner communication, or an external system.

steps.title: 3. Check Workstation Power and Displays
steps.instructions: Verify the workstation, monitors, and externally powered peripherals have normal power and that no loose accessible power connection is present. Expected outcome: Workstation hardware is powered normally.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Data Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible network and scanner-interface cables for secure seating and visible damage. Do not disconnect internal or unidentified system cabling during active operation. Expected outcome: External communication connections are intact.

steps.title: 5. Test Basic Input Devices
steps.instructions: Verify keyboard and mouse operation where safe to do so. Check for an obviously disconnected or failed peripheral. Use an approved known-good replacement only when compatible and permitted. Expected outcome: Peripheral failure is either identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 6. Determine Whether the Problem Is Local or Network-Wide
steps.instructions: Ask whether other networked imaging systems or hospital applications are also experiencing communication problems. If multiple systems are affected, involve IT or network support rather than repeatedly restarting the MRI workstation. Expected outcome: The issue is categorized as scanner-specific or infrastructure-related.

steps.title: 7. Use Only Approved Normal Restart Procedures
steps.instructions: If the patient is clear, data has been protected as much as possible, and manufacturer/facility procedures permit, perform a controlled restart of the affected workstation or system component. Do not repeatedly hard-power-cycle the workstation. Expected outcome: The workstation restarts cleanly and reconnects to the scanner. If normal operation returns and remains stable, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Verify Scanner-to-Workstation Communication
steps.instructions: Confirm patient/exam information can be accessed, scanner status is displayed correctly, and operator commands are communicating normally through the approved interface. Expected outcome: Workstation and scanner communication are restored without recurring disconnects.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the workstation remains responsive through an appropriate nonpatient functional workflow and that no pending warning or communication fault remains. Expected outcome: Operator controls remain stable and the communication path is reliable. If achieved, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Recurrent Freezing or Communication Loss
steps.instructions: If the workstation freezes repeatedly or scanner communication continues to drop after external causes are ruled out, remove the MRI from clinical service until qualified evaluation is completed. Expected outcome: Recurrent failures are escalated rather than temporarily cleared and ignored.

CCR.Complaint: MRI staff reported the operator workstation became unresponsive and lost communication with the scanner.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an accessible workstation network/interface connection was loose.
CCR.Resolution: Secured the connection, performed an approved controlled restart, and verified stable workstation-to-scanner communication through a functional check.

helpfulDetails: What portion of the workstation froze

title: Canon Ultimax-i Fluoroscopy / Interventional System - Calibration or Quality-Control Test Fails
description: Troubleshoots failed calibration or quality-control testing caused by setup, positioning, environmental, accessory, readiness, or repeatability problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patients From Use of an Unverified System
steps.instructions: If a required calibration or quality-control check has failed, do not assume the system remains suitable for clinical imaging. Follow department policy regarding removal from clinical use until the failure is understood. Expected outcome: The system is not used clinically when required performance verification is unresolved.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Failed Test
steps.instructions: Document which calibration or QC procedure failed, the stage at which it failed, displayed messages, and whether the problem is repeatable. Do not substitute an unrelated test as evidence that the failed test is acceptable. Expected outcome: The exact failed verification step is identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Test Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm the correct approved test device, phantom, positioning method, accessories, and normal test workflow were used. Check that the setup has not shifted or been altered. Expected outcome: The test setup matches the facility or manufacturer-approved procedure. If correcting the setup produces a passing result, troubleshooting can stop after repeat verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Positioning and Alignment
steps.instructions: Verify that the test object, detector, table, and imaging geometry are positioned consistently with the approved test method. Remove unintended objects from the imaging field. Expected outcome: Test geometry is correct and repeatable. If alignment correction resolves the failure, document the successful repeat test.

steps.title: 5. Confirm System Readiness
steps.instructions: Verify that the Ultimax-i has completed startup and that acquisition hardware, detector functions, and workstation controls are stable before repeating the test. Expected outcome: The system is fully ready before QC testing begins. If the test now passes reliably, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Relevant External Accessories
steps.instructions: Check test fixtures, cables, positioning aids, external sensors, or other approved accessories used during the procedure for damage, contamination, looseness, or incorrect placement. Expected outcome: Required accessories are intact and correctly connected. If an accessory was responsible, replace it with an approved known-good item and repeat the test.

steps.title: 7. Check Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Look for unusual room temperature, recent power events, construction, vibration, or other environmental changes that may affect consistent imaging or calibration. Do not invent or apply environmental limits not provided by approved documentation. Expected outcome: No obvious external environmental condition is affecting the test.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Approved Test
steps.instructions: Repeat the failed test from the beginning using the approved procedure and unchanged valid conditions. Do not adjust hidden calibration values simply to obtain a pass. Expected outcome: The system completes the required calibration or QC check successfully and repeatably. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the Canon Ultimax-i quality-control imaging test repeatedly failed.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the QC phantom incorrectly positioned relative to the imaging field.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the phantom setup, repeated the approved QC procedure, and verified a successful result.

title: Canon Ultimax-i Fluoroscopy / Interventional System - Cooling, Fan, or Overtemperature Fault Occurs
description: Troubleshoots cooling, fan, or temperature warnings caused by blocked airflow, room conditions, heavy use, contamination, or cooling-system problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Unsafe Operation
steps.instructions: If the system reports an overtemperature condition, produces unusual heat, burning odor, smoke, or abnormal fan noise, stop clinical use when safely possible. Transfer the procedure to alternate equipment when necessary. If smoke, arcing, or burning odor is present, remove power according to emergency procedures and escalate immediately. Expected outcome: The system is no longer operated under potentially unsafe thermal conditions.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Thermal Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint is a displayed temperature warning, unusually loud fan, fan not running, repeated shutdown, excessive cabinet heat, or a condition occurring only after extended operation. Expected outcome: The type and timing of the cooling problem are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect External Airflow
steps.instructions: Check externally accessible ventilation openings for blockage by drapes, covers, equipment, carts, dust buildup, or room objects. Maintain appropriate clearance according to facility and manufacturer guidance. Do not remove covers to access internal fans. Expected outcome: External airflow paths are unobstructed. If clearing a blockage resolves the condition, allow the system to stabilize and continue verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Room Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Determine whether room cooling is operating normally and whether the space is unusually warm. Check for recent HVAC failure, construction, relocated equipment, or heat-producing equipment near the imaging system. Expected outcome: The room environment appears suitable for system operation. Facility HVAC concerns are escalated appropriately.

steps.title: 5. Inspect for Visible Contamination or Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible vents and exterior surfaces for heavy dust, contamination, liquid intrusion, or physical damage that may impair cooling. Use only approved external cleaning methods. Expected outcome: No external contamination or damage is interfering with cooling.

steps.title: 6. Allow the System to Stabilize
steps.instructions: If the fault occurred after sustained operation and no unsafe condition is present, allow the system to cool according to normal operating procedures before restarting. Do not repeatedly clear thermal faults and immediately resume heavy operation. Expected outcome: The system returns to a stable normal temperature state without warning recurrence.

steps.title: 7. Observe Fan and Startup Behavior
steps.instructions: During normal startup, listen for abnormal fan noise, grinding, repeated speed changes, or lack of expected airflow from accessible vents. Do not insert objects into vents or attempt to manipulate internal fans. Expected outcome: Cooling airflow appears normal and no abnormal external indication is present.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Operate the system through an appropriate nonclinical functional check and observe for recurring temperature warnings, unexpected shutdowns, or abnormal fan behavior. Expected outcome: The system remains stable without cooling or overtemperature faults. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the Canon Ultimax-i displayed a temperature warning during operation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external ventilation opening obstructed by stored equipment.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleared the ventilation area, allowed the system to stabilize, and verified normal operation without recurrence of the warning.

title: Canon Ultimax-i Fluoroscopy / Interventional System - Detector or Acquisition Hardware Is Not Ready
description: Troubleshoots detector or acquisition-not-ready conditions caused by startup state, connections, configuration, accessories, communication, or environmental conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Procedure
steps.instructions: If detector or acquisition readiness becomes unreliable during a procedure, do not repeatedly attempt exposures while the patient depends on the system. Maintain clinical continuity using an approved alternate plan. Expected outcome: Patient care does not depend on unreliable acquisition hardware.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Readiness Condition
steps.instructions: Identify what the system reports as unavailable. Note any displayed message, status icon, affected detector or acquisition function, and whether the condition appeared at startup or during use. Expected outcome: The affected acquisition function and timing of the failure are documented. If readiness returns and remains stable, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 3. Verify Complete System Startup
steps.instructions: Confirm that the workstation, imaging system, displays, detector subsystem, and other externally observable components have finished startup. Allow normal initialization to finish before testing. Expected outcome: The system has completed normal startup and is not simply waiting for initialization. If readiness appears normally, troubleshooting can stop after testing.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Detector and Acquisition Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible cables and connectors associated with acquisition hardware for looseness, damage, contamination, strain, or accidental disconnection. Do not disconnect internal or high-voltage components. Expected outcome: All approved external acquisition connections are secure and undamaged. If reseating an accessible connection restores readiness, verify stability and stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify Required Accessories and Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that required external imaging accessories are present, correctly positioned, recognized, and appropriate for the intended examination. Check normal user-accessible acquisition selections for obvious mismatches. Do not change restricted service configuration. Expected outcome: Required accessories and normal acquisition selections are appropriate. If correcting the selection restores readiness, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: 6. Check for External Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect externally accessible detector surfaces, housings, connectors, and cables for impact damage, fluid contamination, bent hardware, or other visible abnormalities. Expected outcome: No physical condition is found that would make continued use unsafe. Damaged hardware is removed from service rather than repeatedly tested.

steps.title: 7. Perform an Approved Restart if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the system is otherwise stable, use the normal shutdown and startup process to reinitialize the acquisition chain. Avoid repeated uncontrolled power cycling. Expected outcome: Acquisition hardware initializes and reaches a stable ready state. If it does, continue with final verification.

steps.title: 8. Verify Acquisition Function Without a Patient
steps.instructions: Using the facility's approved test method, confirm that the acquisition system becomes ready and completes a basic nonclinical imaging check. Verify that the ready condition remains stable. Expected outcome: The detector and acquisition chain remain ready and function consistently. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the Canon Ultimax-i acquisition system remained not ready after room startup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an accessible acquisition cable connection not fully seated.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, restarted the system normally, and verified stable acquisition readiness with a nonclinical functional check.

title: Canon Ultimax-i Fluoroscopy / Interventional System - DICOM, PACS, or Worklist Transfer Fails
description: Troubleshoots failed worklist retrieval or image transfer caused by network connectivity, destination availability, configuration, workflow, or infrastructure issues.

steps.title: 1. Maintain Clinical and Data Continuity
steps.instructions: If network services fail during an active case, ensure images and study information are preserved locally when supported and follow departmental downtime procedures. Do not delete or repeatedly resend studies without understanding their status. Expected outcome: Patient imaging data is protected while network troubleshooting is performed.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Function Is Failing
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem affects modality worklist retrieval, DICOM image transfer, PACS receipt, query/retrieve functions, or all network communication. Record any displayed network or transfer message and whether the issue affects one study or every study. Expected outcome: The specific failing communication path is identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Local Network Connectivity
steps.instructions: Check accessible network cables, connectors, and link indications where available. Look for loose, damaged, or recently moved connections. Do not change network addresses or configuration simply to test connectivity. Expected outcome: The physical network connection appears intact. If restoring an external connection resolves communication, verify transfers and stop.

steps.title: 4. Determine Whether the Issue Is Device-Specific
steps.instructions: Check whether other imaging systems or workstations in the same area can access the affected PACS, worklist, or network service. Coordinate with IT when appropriate. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to the Ultimax-i or to a broader network/server outage.

steps.title: 5. Verify Normal Network Configuration
steps.instructions: Review user-accessible or documented configuration information without changing values. Confirm that no recent approved network change, room move, server migration, or maintenance event could explain the failure. Do not alter IP, destination, port, or DICOM parameters without authorization and known-good configuration information. Expected outcome: The observed configuration is consistent with the expected environment or a discrepancy is identified for authorized correction.

steps.title: 6. Check Study and Workflow Information
steps.instructions: For a single-study problem, verify that the study is complete enough for transfer and that required patient or examination information is present. Check whether the failure follows one specific record or all records. Expected outcome: A workflow-specific issue is distinguished from a general network failure.

steps.title: 7. Test the Affected Communication Path
steps.instructions: When appropriate, use an approved test study or nonclinical workflow to verify worklist retrieval or DICOM transfer. Confirm receipt at the intended destination rather than relying only on a local "sent" indication. Expected outcome: The destination receives the expected data successfully. If confirmed, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Verify End-to-End Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm the complete path from the Ultimax-i through the network to the intended worklist or PACS destination. Verify that new communication remains reliable. Expected outcome: Worklist and/or image transfer functions normally end to end. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that studies from the Canon Ultimax-i were not transferring to PACS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external network cable at the workstation not fully seated.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection and verified successful transfer and PACS receipt of a nonclinical test study.

helpfulDetails: Function affected: worklist, PACS, or both
One study or all studies affected

title: Canon Ultimax-i Fluoroscopy / Interventional System - Exposure or Scan Will Not Start or Is Aborted
description: Troubleshoots exposures that will not initiate or terminate unexpectedly because of readiness, controls, interlocks, accessories, settings, or communication.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Before Repeating Exposure Attempts
steps.instructions: Do not repeatedly attempt exposures simply to see whether the problem clears. If imaging is required for an ongoing procedure and the Ultimax-i is unreliable, move to an approved alternate imaging plan. Expected outcome: Unnecessary radiation exposure is avoided and clinical continuity is maintained.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether exposure never starts, begins and immediately aborts, stops during acquisition, or fails only in a particular imaging mode. Record any displayed message and the point in the workflow where the failure occurs. Expected outcome: The failure is reproducible and clearly defined. If normal imaging resumes, proceed to final verification before returning to use.

steps.title: 3. Verify System Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm that the system has completed startup and that the acquisition hardware, detector, positioning components, and workstation show normal readiness.
