Expected outcome: No upstream not-ready condition is preventing exposure. If resolving a readiness issue restores imaging, stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Check External Exposure Controls
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible hand switches, footswitches, control-panel buttons, and external cables used to initiate fluoroscopy or acquisition. Look for damage, contamination, loose connections, or a control that does not respond normally. Use a known-good approved accessory when available and appropriate. Expected outcome: The external exposure control operates normally. If substitution identifies a defective accessory, replace or remove it from service and verify operation.

steps.title: 5. Check Safety Interlocks and Positioning Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify that no active emergency stop, collision condition, positioning issue, or other externally apparent safety state is inhibiting exposure. Confirm that required positioning is complete and stable. Never bypass an interlock. Expected outcome: The system is in a normal condition permitting exposure. If correcting the external condition restores imaging, proceed to verification.

steps.title: 6. Review Normal Examination Selections
steps.instructions: Check that the intended examination, imaging mode, detector selection, and other operator-accessible settings are appropriate and complete. Do not alter restricted service or calibration parameters. Expected outcome: The selected imaging workflow is internally consistent and ready to run. If correcting an obvious selection error resolves the issue, verify and stop.

steps.title: 7. Check for Communication or Workstation Symptoms
steps.instructions: Determine whether the exposure problem occurs alongside frozen controls, delayed responses, detector-not-ready status, communication warnings, or other workstation abnormalities. If the system software is unstable, perform only an approved normal restart when clinically safe. Expected outcome: The workstation and acquisition system respond normally. If restart restores stable operation, continue to final testing.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Nonclinical Functional Test
steps.instructions: Using an approved test setup, verify that an exposure or acquisition can be initiated and completed without abnormal termination. Confirm that the system returns to ready status afterward. Expected outcome: Imaging starts, completes, and returns to ready status consistently. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that fluoroscopic exposure on the Canon Ultimax-i would not initiate from the foot control.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external footswitch connector partially disconnected.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the footswitch connection and verified reliable exposure initiation and completion using an approved nonclinical test setup.

title: Canon Ultimax-i Fluoroscopy / Interventional System - Gantry, Table, or Positioning Motion Is Unavailable
description: Troubleshoots unavailable or inhibited positioning caused by obstructions, controls, interlocks, positioning limits, connections, or system readiness.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Before Testing Motion
steps.instructions: Stop attempted movement if the patient, staff, lines, accessories, or procedural equipment could be trapped, pulled, struck, or displaced. If the system cannot be positioned reliably during a procedure, transition to an alternate safe workflow. Never troubleshoot unpredictable movement while a patient depends on the system. Expected outcome: The patient and surrounding equipment are protected from unintended motion. Continue only when movement can be tested safely.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Motion Is Affected
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem affects the table, imaging assembly, specific directional movement, or all positioning functions. Confirm whether movement is completely unavailable, intermittent, limited, or stops at a particular position. Expected outcome: The affected motion function and exact symptom are identified. If the system operates normally during testing, verify all required motion functions and stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Physical Obstructions
steps.instructions: Check around and beneath the table and imaging system for stools, cables, foot controls, carts, patient lines, drapes, accessories, or other objects interfering with travel. Do not force movement against resistance. Expected outcome: The full intended travel path is clear. If removal of an obstruction restores motion, verify safe operation and stop.

steps.title: 4. Check Emergency Stops and Safety Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify that emergency-stop controls and accessible motion-safety controls are in their normal states. Confirm that no obvious collision, safety, or positioning condition is preventing movement. Only reset a safety control after determining why it was activated. Expected outcome: No active external safety condition is inhibiting movement. If motion returns after resolving the condition, perform functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Verify Controls and Operating State
steps.instructions: Confirm that the system has completed startup and is in an operating state that permits positioning. Test the appropriate operator-accessible positioning controls and note whether one control station works while another does not. Expected outcome: Motion commands are accepted from functioning controls. If a single external control was the problem and normal motion is restored, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Accessible Control Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible footswitches, hand controls, pendants, and associated external cables or connectors when relevant. Look for damage, pinching, contamination, looseness, or accidental disconnection. Use an approved known-good accessory only when compatibility is established. Expected outcome: External positioning controls and cables are intact and connected. If a known-good compatible control restores operation, identify the defective accessory and stop after testing.

steps.title: 7. Check Position and Travel Conditions
steps.instructions: Determine whether the system is already at a normal travel boundary or in a position where a different movement must occur before the requested movement becomes available. Do not override software or mechanical limits. Expected outcome: The requested motion is being attempted within normal accessible positioning conditions. If repositioning within normal controls restores motion, verify repeatability and stop.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Motion Verification
steps.instructions: Without a patient, exercise the affected positioning function through an appropriate safe range using normal controls. Verify smooth response, predictable stopping, and absence of abnormal noise, binding, or repeated interruption. Expected outcome: Positioning operates smoothly and consistently. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that table positioning on the Canon Ultimax-i was unavailable during room setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an equipment cable routed into the table travel area and interfering with movement.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering rerouted the cable, confirmed the travel path was clear, and verified smooth table movement using normal controls.

helpfulDetails: Direction or position where motion stops
Objects or cables in travel path

title: Canon Ultimax-i Fluoroscopy / Interventional System - Image Quality Is Poor or Artifacts Are Present
description: Troubleshoots poor image quality or artifacts caused by positioning, accessories, contamination, technique, display conditions, detector issues, or environmental factors.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient From Unnecessary Repeat Imaging
steps.instructions: If poor image quality could lead to repeated exposures, stop clinical troubleshooting and use an approved test object or phantom whenever possible. If diagnostic imaging cannot be obtained reliably, use alternate equipment. Expected outcome: Additional patient exposure is minimized while the image-quality problem is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Artifact or Image Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves noise, lines, shading, nonuniformity, distortion, clipping, motion blur, poor contrast, localized artifacts, or another visible problem. Establish whether it occurs in fluoroscopy, acquisition, all modes, or only certain positioning. Expected outcome: The image-quality complaint is clearly characterized and reproducible.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Imaging Field
steps.instructions: Check for external objects within or near the beam path, including cables, table accessories, pads, positioning devices, clips, tools, drapes, protective equipment, or other radiopaque materials. Expected outcome: No unintended object is contributing to the image. If removal resolves the artifact, verify with a test image and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Imaging Surfaces
steps.instructions: Inspect detector covers and other accessible surfaces for dirt, fluid residue, damage, attached materials, or objects that could affect imaging. Clean only according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: Accessible imaging surfaces are clean and intact. If cleaning removes the artifact, verify and stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify Patient or Test-Object Positioning
steps.instructions: Check centering, orientation, motion, geometry, and positioning of the patient or approved test object. Confirm the artifact is not caused by movement or inappropriate placement. Expected outcome: Positioning is appropriate and repeatable. If corrected positioning restores acceptable images, troubleshooting can stop after confirmation.

steps.title: 6. Review Normal Imaging Selections
steps.instructions: Verify that the selected examination and user-accessible image-processing or acquisition settings are appropriate for the intended task. Compare the issue with a known normal workflow when possible. Do not alter calibration or restricted service parameters. Expected outcome: Normal imaging settings are appropriate. If an incorrect selection caused the problem, restore the correct configuration and verify images.

steps.title: 7. Compare Across Modes or Positions
steps.instructions: Using an approved phantom or test object, determine whether the artifact follows a specific acquisition mode, detector position, field location, or geometry. This helps separate external positioning problems from persistent equipment-related image defects. Expected outcome: The artifact is either eliminated through an external correction or shown to persist consistently under controlled testing.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Image-Quality Verification
steps.instructions: Acquire appropriate nonclinical test images and confirm that the reported artifact is absent and image quality is consistent with normal system performance and departmental expectations. Expected outcome: Test images are free from the reported abnormality. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported a repeatable artifact appearing on Canon Ultimax-i images.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a radiopaque positioning accessory unintentionally remaining within the imaging field.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the accessory and verified normal artifact-free imaging using an approved test object.

helpfulDetails: Position or field where it appears

title: Canon Ultimax-i Fluoroscopy / Interventional System - Study Will Not Save, Reconstruct, or Export
description: Troubleshoots study-processing failures caused by workflow state, storage, workstation responsiveness, patient information, destination availability, or communication problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Data and Clinical Continuity
steps.instructions: Do not delete, overwrite, or repeatedly manipulate a study that may contain the only copy of clinically important images. Confirm that necessary imaging data is preserved locally when possible and follow departmental downtime procedures. Expected outcome: Existing patient data is protected before troubleshooting begins.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Operation Is Failing
steps.instructions: Determine whether the study cannot be saved locally, reconstruction does not complete, export fails, or the system reports that the study is incomplete. Record any displayed message and whether the issue affects one study or every study. Expected outcome: The exact workflow stage and scope of the failure are identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Workstation Responsiveness
steps.instructions: Confirm that the workstation is responding normally and that the problem is not part of a larger freeze or communication failure. Check whether other studies can be opened or normal user functions can be completed. Expected outcome: The workstation is either confirmed stable or identified as part of the problem.

steps.title: 4. Review Study Information and Workflow
steps.instructions: Verify that required patient and examination information is present and that the study has been completed through the normal clinical workflow. Compare the affected study with a known normal workflow without changing protected clinical data unnecessarily. Expected outcome: No obvious incomplete workflow or missing information is preventing processing. If completing the proper workflow resolves the problem, verify and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Local Storage or System Messages
steps.instructions: Review normal user-accessible indicators for storage or processing warnings. Do not delete clinical studies or clear storage solely to create space without following approved data-retention procedures. Expected outcome: No obvious user-accessible storage condition is preventing save or reconstruction.

steps.title: 6. Check Export Destination Availability
steps.instructions: If local saving succeeds but export fails, verify the intended destination is available and that network connectivity is intact. Check whether another study can be transferred through the same route. Expected outcome: The problem is narrowed to local processing or external export communication.

steps.title: 7. Use an Approved Restart When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the workstation is stable enough to protect existing data and normal procedures permit, complete a controlled application or system restart. Avoid forced shutdown during active saving, reconstruction, or export. Expected outcome: Processing services restart normally without loss of stored data.

steps.title: 8. Verify With a Nonclinical Test Study
steps.instructions: Using an approved test workflow, confirm that a new study can be saved, processed or reconstructed as applicable, and exported to the intended destination. Confirm destination receipt when export is tested. Expected outcome: Study processing and export complete successfully end to end. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that studies acquired on the Canon Ultimax-i would save locally but would not export to PACS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the workstation's external network connection loose, preventing communication with the destination.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the network connection and verified successful export and PACS receipt of a nonclinical test study.

helpfulDetails: Save, reconstruct, or export function affected
One study or all studies affected

title: Canon Ultimax-i Fluoroscopy / Interventional System - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Troubleshoots loss of power, incomplete startup, or unavailable system operation caused by external power, connections, controls, or startup conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: If the Ultimax-i is supporting an active procedure and becomes unreliable, stop using it for patient care when clinically safe. Move the patient or procedure to another verified imaging system according to departmental procedures. Do not continue troubleshooting while a patient depends on unreliable imaging, positioning, monitoring, or procedural support. Expected outcome: Patient care is safely transferred or delayed before technical troubleshooting begins. If continuity of care is secured, continue.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the system is completely dead, partially powered, stuck during startup, repeatedly restarting, or displaying a message. Note which consoles, monitors, indicators, or system components have power. Ask whether the problem followed a facility outage, emergency-power transfer, shutdown, service activity, or abnormal restart. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly categorized as no power, partial power, or incomplete startup. If normal startup completes during verification, troubleshooting can stop after functional testing.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility Power
steps.instructions: Confirm that the room has normal electrical service and that applicable facility disconnects or supplied power controls are in their normal operating state. Check for evidence that other equipment on the same electrical distribution is affected. Do not reset facility breakers repeatedly or bypass electrical protection. Expected outcome: Required facility power is available and no obvious room-level electrical problem is present. If restoring an approved external power condition corrects startup, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Power Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible power cords, plugs, connectors, and external power interfaces associated with the operator workstation and related system equipment. Look for looseness, damage, overheating, contamination, or evidence of accidental disconnection. Do not open covers or access energized internal power assemblies. Expected outcome: Accessible power connections are secure and undamaged. If reseating an approved external connection restores normal startup, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Check Emergency Stops and Safety Interlocks
steps.instructions: Verify that accessible emergency-stop controls have not been activated and that obvious room or equipment safety interlocks are in their normal state. Reset an emergency stop only when the cause of activation is known and the area is safe. Expected outcome: No active external safety control is intentionally preventing system operation. If correcting the condition restores startup, continue with functional verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Startup Sequence and Connected Components
steps.instructions: Confirm that normal operator-accessible system components are powered and started in the expected sequence. Check whether the acquisition workstation, displays, positioning system, and imaging components reach their normal ready states. Avoid repeated power cycling. Use only normal shutdown and restart functions available to Clinical Engineering. Expected outcome: All externally observable system components complete startup normally. If they do, the issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Check for Environmental or Infrastructure Problems
steps.instructions: Inspect the room for abnormal heat, water intrusion, construction activity, unusual odor, excessive dust, blocked external ventilation, or indications of a facility electrical or cooling problem. If burning odor, smoke, liquid intrusion, arcing, or abnormal heat is present, disconnect from use and escalate immediately. Expected outcome: The environment is suitable for equipment operation. Any identified facility issue is corrected before another startup attempt.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction, complete a normal startup and verify that the system reaches its normal ready state without repeated errors or unexpected resets. Verify basic operator interface, positioning availability, and imaging readiness without exposing a patient. Expected outcome: The Ultimax-i starts consistently and all required subsystems become available. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Canon Ultimax-i would not complete startup and remained unavailable for imaging.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an accessible system power connection loose following room activity.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, restarted the system normally, and verified successful startup and basic imaging-system readiness.

helpfulDetails: Exact startup behavior or displayed message
Components that did or did not power on
Recent outage or room electrical event

title: Canon Ultimax-i Fluoroscopy / Interventional System - Workstation Freezes or Loses Communication
description: Troubleshoots frozen controls, unavailable workstation functions, or subsystem communication loss caused by connections, software state, network, power, or external infrastructure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Procedure
steps.instructions: If the workstation freezes or loses communication during clinical use, do not depend on uncertain imaging or control functions. Follow the department's safe procedure interruption or alternate-equipment plan. Expected outcome: Patient care is no longer dependent on an unstable workstation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm What Has Frozen or Disconnected
steps.instructions: Determine whether the entire workstation is unresponsive, only one application is affected, images have stopped updating, acquisition hardware is disconnected, or another subsystem is reporting loss of communication. Record displayed messages and the last successful action. Expected outcome: The affected portion of the system is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Check Basic Power and Display Status
steps.instructions: Confirm that the workstation, displays, and externally powered peripherals remain on. Verify that the problem is not simply a powered-off display, loose power connection, or disconnected peripheral. Expected outcome: Required external workstation hardware has power. If restoring an external power connection corrects the issue, verify stability and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Communication Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible Ethernet, data, USB, display, and other external connections relevant to the affected workstation or subsystem. Check for loose plugs, damaged cables, or recent room activity. Do not disturb internal system wiring. Expected outcome: External communication connections are secure. If reconnection restores communication, verify continued operation and stop.

steps.title: 5. Determine Whether the Problem Is Local or Infrastructure-Related
steps.instructions: Check whether only the Ultimax-i workstation is affected or whether other room or hospital systems are also experiencing network or communication problems. Expected outcome: The failure is categorized as device-local or potentially infrastructure-related.

steps.title: 6. Allow Normal Application Recovery When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the system provides an approved normal method to close or restart an affected application, use it only when patient care is protected and no data-integrity concern is present. Avoid forced shutdown unless normal methods are unavailable and facility procedures permit it. Expected outcome: The application returns to normal operation without recurring communication loss.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled System Restart if Needed
steps.instructions: When appropriate, complete the normal system shutdown and restart sequence. Observe whether all acquisition and communication functions reconnect normally. Expected outcome: The workstation completes startup and reconnects to required system components. If communication remains stable, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Verify Workstation and Acquisition Functions
steps.instructions: Without a patient, confirm responsive controls, acquisition readiness, image display, and the specific communication path that previously failed. Expected outcome: The workstation remains responsive and required communications are stable. If successful, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Canon Ultimax-i workstation stopped responding and lost communication with the imaging system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an accessible data connection at the workstation loose.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, completed a normal restart, and verified stable workstation response and acquisition communication.

title: Canon Alphenix Sky+ Angiography System - Accessory, Catheter, or Module Is Not Recognized
description: Troubleshoot compatible accessories, catheter-related interfaces, or modules that are connected but unavailable, intermittently recognized, or reported as disconnected.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Procedure
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an accessory or module while a patient depends on its function. If recognition is lost during a procedure, establish a safe clinical alternative before manipulating connections. Expected outcome: The patient is not dependent on the affected accessory or module.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Unrecognized Component
steps.instructions: Determine the accessory, catheter-related interface, module, or connected device involved and record the exact system indication. Expected outcome: The affected component and recognition failure are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Compatibility and Intended Use
steps.instructions: Confirm that the connected component is approved and appropriate for the intended system function. Do not force connectors or use unapproved adapters to obtain recognition. Expected outcome: The component is suitable for use with the system and current function.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Component and Connector
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible connector surfaces, housings, cables, strain reliefs, latches, and contacts for contamination, physical damage, bent components, fluid exposure, or wear. Expected outcome: No visible defect prevents reliable connection. Damaged components are removed from service.

steps.title: 5. Reseat the Connection
steps.instructions: Reconnect the accessory or module using its normal approved connection and confirm that locking or retaining features fully engage. Expected outcome: The component becomes recognized and remains connected. If recognition is stable, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Required External Power
steps.instructions: If the accessory or module has an independent approved power source, confirm that it is powered and indicates normal operation. Expected outcome: The connected component is not unavailable because of an external power problem.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Component
steps.instructions: When available, connect a known-good compatible accessory, cable, interface, or module. Expected outcome: Recognition of the known-good component isolates the original accessory or module as the likely cause.

steps.title: 8. Test the Component Through Normal Positioning
steps.instructions: Verify recognition while the system, cable, accessory, or table is placed through normal expected positions without stressing the connection. Expected outcome: Recognition remains stable throughout normal operation.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Recognition Failure
steps.instructions: If known-good compatible components are not recognized or recognition repeatedly drops out, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The affected interface remains out of clinical service pending qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that an accessory module connected to the Canon Alphenix Sky+ was not recognized.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found contamination on the accessible external connector and confirmed normal recognition after approved cleaning and reconnection.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned and reseated the connection, verified stable module recognition through normal positioning, and returned the function to service.

title: Canon Alphenix Sky+ Angiography System - Battery Will Not Charge or Runtime Is Short
description: Troubleshoot battery-backed system components or supported backup power that will not charge, reports low capacity, or provides unexpectedly short runtime.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient From Unexpected Power Loss
steps.instructions: Do not rely on a battery-backed component or backup-power function with uncertain runtime during a procedure. Ensure stable facility power and an appropriate contingency before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient care is protected from an unexpected loss of power.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Battery-Backed Component
steps.instructions: Determine exactly which supported system component, mobile accessory, control, or backup-power device is reporting a charging or runtime problem. Record its indicators or messages. Expected outcome: The complaint is tied to a specific battery-backed component rather than the angiography system generally.

steps.title: 3. Verify Charging Power
steps.instructions: Confirm that the affected component is connected to its approved charging source and that facility power is available. Inspect accessible charging cords, power supplies, docks, and connections. Expected outcome: The charging source is available and connections are secure.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Battery or External Power Accessory
steps.instructions: Where externally accessible without disassembly, inspect the battery, charging interface, dock, or power accessory for swelling, leakage, heat, damaged contacts, cracked housings, contamination, or other abnormality. Expected outcome: No visible battery hazard is present. Any swollen, leaking, overheated, or damaged battery is immediately removed from service and handled per facility procedure.

steps.title: 5. Confirm Charging Indication
steps.instructions: Reconnect the device to its approved charger and verify that the expected charging or external-power indication appears. Expected outcome: The component recognizes the charging source and begins charging.

steps.title: 6. Allow an Appropriate Charge Cycle
steps.instructions: If the battery was deeply discharged, allow charging according to approved manufacturer guidance before evaluating runtime. Do not infer battery failure solely from a brief initial charge attempt. Expected outcome: Battery charge status increases normally.

steps.title: 7. Compare With Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Where appropriate, test with a known-good approved charger, cable, dock, or replaceable battery to isolate the affected component. Expected outcome: The substitution identifies whether the problem follows the battery/accessory or remains with the equipment.

steps.title: 8. Verify Runtime Using Approved Testing
steps.instructions: If runtime testing is appropriate for the specific battery-backed component, evaluate it using the manufacturer-approved method or applicable service procedure. Expected outcome: Runtime meets the applicable service requirement. If charging and runtime are acceptable, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Unacceptable Battery Performance
steps.instructions: If charging remains abnormal, runtime fails approved criteria, or the component cannot reliably maintain backup power, remove it from service. Expected outcome: An unreliable battery-backed function is not used for patient care.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that a battery-backed Canon Alphenix Sky+ system accessory would not maintain charge.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the approved charging cable damaged and confirmed normal charging with a known-good compatible cable.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the damaged charging cable, verified normal charge indication and applicable battery operation, and returned the accessory to service.

helpfulDetails: Any abnormal heat, odor, or swelling

title: Canon Alphenix Sky+ Angiography System - Display, Controls, or Alarm Audio Fails
description: Troubleshoot blank or abnormal displays, unresponsive controls, failed audible indications, loose connections, settings, or system communication problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Unsafe Operation
steps.instructions: Do not continue using the angiography system if required displays, controls, or audible safety indications are unavailable or unreliable during patient care. Expected outcome: The patient is moved to a safe alternative workflow before troubleshooting affects clinical operation.

steps.title: 2. Define the Failed Function
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem affects one display, all displays, a specific operator control, touchscreen, keyboard, foot control, hand control, or audible indication. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to a specific interface or identified as a broader system failure.

steps.title: 3. Check Overall System Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the rest of the system is powered and responsive. Observe system status indicators and determine whether the affected interface alone is unavailable. Expected outcome: The failure is separated into an isolated interface issue or a system-wide condition.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Connections
steps.instructions: Check display cables, control cables, external interface connections, accessory controls, and approved power connections for looseness, damage, or strain. Expected outcome: External connections are secure and undamaged.

steps.title: 5. Verify Accessible Display and Audio Settings
steps.instructions: Check normal user-accessible brightness, display selection, audio level, mute status, and related operating settings where applicable. Do not change restricted configuration. Expected outcome: The failure is not caused by an accessible setting. Correcting the setting restores function if it was the cause.

steps.title: 6. Check for Obstruction or Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect touch surfaces, control panels, switches, and external controls for covers, contamination, fluid residue, or physical obstruction that could interfere with operation. Expected outcome: Controls are clean, unobstructed, and mechanically usable.

steps.title: 7. Compare or Substitute External Components
steps.instructions: Where compatible components are externally interchangeable, test with a known-good control, display connection, cable, or peripheral as appropriate. Expected outcome: The substitution identifies an external component failure or confirms that the problem remains with the system.

steps.title: 8. Perform an Approved Restart
steps.instructions: With the patient safely separated from the equipment and no evidence of physical or electrical damage, perform a normal system restart. Expected outcome: Displays, controls, and audible indications initialize normally. If all required functions remain stable, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 9. Verify Required Safety Functions
steps.instructions: Confirm the affected controls respond consistently and verify required audible and visual system indications using appropriate functional testing. Expected outcome: User interfaces and required indications function reliably before clinical use.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Any Persistent Interface Failure
steps.instructions: If a required display, control, or alarm-related audio function remains unreliable, remove the system from service. Expected outcome: Equipment with an unreliable operator or safety interface is not returned to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that one operator display on the Canon Alphenix Sky+ was blank while the rest of the system remained powered.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external display connection loose at the accessible interface.

title: Canon Alphenix Sky+ Angiography System - Measurement Is Inaccurate or Will Not Calibrate
description: Troubleshoot questionable measurements or calibration failures caused by accessories, setup, positioning, configuration, environment, or service-level system problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient From Unreliable Measurements
steps.instructions: Do not use a measurement known or suspected to be inaccurate for clinical decisions. Use an alternate verified measurement method when the value is clinically required. Expected outcome: Patient care does not depend on the questionable measurement.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Measurement Problem
steps.instructions: Identify the exact measurement or calibration function involved, the circumstances under which the discrepancy occurs, and any displayed calibration failure message. Expected outcome: The problem is defined well enough to reproduce or objectively evaluate.

steps.title: 3. Verify External Setup
steps.instructions: Inspect relevant cables, sensors, modules, accessories, phantoms, reference devices, or positioning aids used for the measurement or approved calibration process. Expected outcome: Required external components are correctly connected, intact, and positioned.

steps.title: 4. Confirm Correct Configuration and Selection
steps.instructions: Verify normal user-accessible settings, selected input, measurement mode, accessory selection, and other visible configuration relevant to the test. Do not alter restricted service parameters. Expected outcome: The system is configured for the intended measurement.

steps.title: 5. Check Positioning and Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm that patient, table, detector, reference object, sensor, or other relevant components are positioned appropriately for the measurement. Check for obvious environmental or mechanical conditions that could invalidate the test. Expected outcome: The measurement setup is repeatable and free from obvious external errors.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Known-Good Reference
steps.instructions: When appropriate and within Clinical Engineering scope, compare the reported measurement with approved test equipment or another known-good reference suitable for the function being evaluated. Expected outcome: The discrepancy is objectively confirmed or shown to be within the expected behavior defined by applicable service documentation.

steps.title: 7. Repeat Only Approved Calibration Procedures
steps.instructions: If calibration is within normal authorized Clinical Engineering scope, repeat the manufacturer-approved calibration or verification procedure using the specified setup and approved equipment. Do not enter unauthorized service menus. Expected outcome: Calibration completes successfully and verification results are acceptable. If so, troubleshooting can stop after final testing.

steps.title: 8. Verify Repeatability
steps.instructions: Repeat the relevant measurement or verification sufficiently to confirm that the corrected result is stable rather than a one-time pass. Expected outcome: The system produces consistent, verified measurements.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Inaccuracy or Calibration Failure
steps.instructions: If measurements remain questionable or an approved calibration cannot be completed, remove the affected function or system from service. Expected outcome: An unverified measurement function is not used clinically.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that a measurement displayed by the Canon Alphenix Sky+ was inconsistent with the expected value.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external measurement accessory improperly seated and obtained normal comparison results after reseating it.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the accessory, repeated the applicable verification, confirmed stable results, and returned the system to service.

title: Canon Alphenix Sky+ Angiography System - Network, Patient Record, or Data Export Fails
description: Troubleshoot network connectivity, patient information exchange, image or data transfer, and export failures caused by connections, destinations, configuration, or infrastructure.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Data Integrity
steps.instructions: If network or patient-record communication fails during a procedure, follow the facility's approved downtime workflow. Do not alter identifiers or repeatedly resend data without understanding the destination state. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely and duplicate or mismatched records are avoided.

steps.title: 2. Define the Communication Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue affects network connectivity, patient worklist or record information, image transfer, data export, one destination, or all destinations. Record exact messages and timestamps. Expected outcome: The communication failure is narrowed to a specific function and destination.

steps.title: 3. Verify Local Network Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible Ethernet or approved network connections for looseness, damage, or disconnection. Observe available link indicators without changing network configuration. Expected outcome: The physical connection appears intact and network link is present where applicable.

steps.title: 4. Check the Scope of the Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether other network functions on the system work and whether other devices in the same area can reach the relevant clinical system. Expected outcome: The problem is classified as device-specific, destination-specific, or potentially infrastructure-wide.

steps.title: 5. Verify Patient and Destination Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm that the correct patient, study, destination, or export target has been selected using normal clinical controls. Do not modify protected network parameters merely to test connectivity. Expected outcome: The transfer is being attempted with the intended patient context and destination.

steps.title: 6. Check External Export Media or Accessories
steps.instructions: If the failure involves approved removable media or another export accessory, inspect the media and interface and test with a known-good approved alternative when appropriate. Expected outcome: External export media or accessories are confirmed functional or identified as the cause.

steps.title: 7. Verify Accessible Network Configuration Without Changing It
steps.instructions: Record visible network status and configuration information that Clinical Engineering is authorized to view. Compare it with documented site records when available. Do not make unapproved IP, VLAN, destination, or security changes. Expected outcome: No obvious discrepancy exists, or a documented configuration problem is identified for correction through the appropriate process.

steps.title: 8. Coordinate With IT or Integration Support
steps.instructions: If physical connectivity is intact but communication remains unavailable, provide IT or application support with the affected system, destination, timestamp, network status, and exact failure behavior. Expected outcome: Infrastructure, server, interface, firewall, routing, or destination-system causes can be evaluated without unnecessary changes to the medical device.

steps.title: 9. Verify End-to-End Communication
steps.instructions: After correction, perform an approved test that confirms data reaches the intended destination and is associated with the correct patient or test record. Expected outcome: The complete communication path operates correctly. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Recurrent or Unresolved Communication Failure
steps.instructions: If communication remains unreliable or the system loses data connectivity repeatedly, remove the affected network-dependent function from service and escalate appropriately. Expected outcome: Unreliable data exchange is not represented as functional.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Canon Alphenix Sky+ could not send study data to the configured clinical destination.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the accessible network cable disconnected at the system connection and confirmed network link after reconnection.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reconnected the cable, verified network communication and successful test transfer to the intended destination, and returned the network function to service.

title: Canon Alphenix Sky+ Angiography System - Patient Cable, Lead, or Sensor Is Not Detected
description: Troubleshoot patient-interface cables, leads, sensors, or related monitoring accessories that are connected but absent, intermittently detected, or unavailable.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Monitoring
steps.instructions: If the affected cable, lead, or sensor provides clinically important monitoring, do not troubleshoot it while the patient depends on unreliable data. Establish an alternate verified monitoring method first. Expected outcome: Required patient monitoring remains available independently of the affected connection.

steps.title: 2. Confirm What Is Not Being Detected
steps.instructions: Identify the exact cable, lead, sensor, or patient-interface accessory involved. Determine whether it is never detected, becomes disconnected intermittently, or is recognized only in certain positions. Expected outcome: The failure is reproduced and associated with a specific accessory, connection, or function.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Patient Accessory
steps.instructions: Check the cable, lead, sensor, connector shell, strain relief, pins or contacts that are safely visible, and any detachable sections for contamination, bending, cracks, cuts, fluid intrusion, or other damage. Expected outcome: The accessory is clean, intact, and suitable for further testing. Damaged accessories are removed from use.

steps.title: 4. Reseat All Accessible Connections
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect the affected accessory using normal approved connections. Verify full seating at the patient interface, intermediate connection, and system connection where applicable. Expected outcome: The accessory is securely connected and recognized. If detection remains stable, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Verify Correct Accessory Type and Placement
steps.instructions: Confirm that the connected cable, lead, or sensor is appropriate for the intended system function and is installed or positioned correctly. Avoid forcing incompatible connectors. Expected outcome: The correct accessory is being used in the correct connection and position.

steps.title: 6. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Accessory
steps.instructions: When available, replace the suspect cable, lead, or sensor with a known-good compatible accessory approved for the system. Expected outcome: If the known-good accessory is detected normally, the original accessory is the likely cause and should remain out of service.

steps.title: 7. Compare Available Connections
steps.instructions: If the system design permits normal user-accessible connection changes, test another approved connection or equivalent interface without changing restricted configuration. Expected outcome: The test helps separate an accessory problem from a particular external connection or system-level issue.

steps.title: 8. Verify Stable Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm that the accessory remains continuously detected during normal positioning and movement expected in clinical use. Verify the associated displayed signal or status. Expected outcome: Detection remains stable and the patient-interface function operates normally.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Detection Failure
steps.instructions: If multiple known-good compatible accessories are not detected or detection remains intermittent, discontinue external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The affected system function remains out of clinical use pending qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that a patient monitoring cable connected to the Canon Alphenix Sky+ was not being detected.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found damage at the accessory cable strain relief and confirmed normal detection with a known-good compatible cable.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the damaged cable, verified stable detection and signal display, and returned the affected function to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact cable, lead, or sensor involved

title: Canon Alphenix Sky+ Angiography System - Signal Is Noisy, Intermittent, or Missing
description: Troubleshoot unstable or missing patient-related signals caused by accessories, connections, positioning, interference, patient interface, or system communication.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Verify Alternate Monitoring
steps.instructions: Do not rely on an intermittent or noisy signal for clinical decision-making. Establish another verified monitoring method when the affected signal is clinically important. Expected outcome: Clinical monitoring remains reliable while troubleshooting proceeds.

steps.title: 2. Define the Signal Problem
steps.instructions: Identify the exact signal involved and determine whether it is completely absent, noisy, intermittent, position-dependent, or lost only during system or table movement. Expected outcome: The symptom is clearly defined and can be compared before and after each corrective action.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Patient Connections and Accessories
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible leads, sensors, cables, adapters, connectors, electrodes or other patient-interface accessories applicable to the affected signal. Look for loose connections, contamination, damaged insulation, worn contacts, or strain. Expected outcome: Patient-interface components are intact and firmly connected.

steps.title: 4. Verify Patient Interface and Positioning
steps.instructions: Check that applicable leads, sensors, or electrodes are positioned appropriately and have adequate contact. Ensure cables are not stretched, trapped, sharply bent, or routed where normal system movement pulls on them. Expected outcome: Patient-interface conditions support a stable signal.

steps.title: 5. Separate Motion From Equipment Failure
steps.instructions: Observe whether signal degradation corresponds with patient movement, cable movement, table movement, detector movement, or another repeatable physical condition. Expected outcome: A movement-related external cause is identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 6. Check for Environmental Interference
steps.instructions: Look for recently added or relocated electrical equipment, damaged power accessories, poorly routed signal cables, or other obvious environmental conditions associated with the onset of noise. Expected outcome: No readily correctable external interference source remains.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Use a known-good compatible cable, sensor, lead set, adapter, or other relevant accessory when available. Expected outcome: A stable signal with the known-good accessory identifies the original accessory as the likely cause. Troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Verify Signal Stability
steps.instructions: Observe the signal long enough to confirm that it remains present and stable through normal positioning and expected system movement. Expected outcome: The signal remains consistently available without unexplained noise or dropouts.

steps.title: 9. Escalate an Unresolved Signal Problem
steps.instructions: If the problem persists with verified connections and known-good accessories, remove the affected function from service and escalate. Expected outcome: An unreliable signal is not returned to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported an intermittent patient signal on the Canon Alphenix Sky+ during room setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a patient cable with an intermittent connection near its external connector and reproduced the signal loss by gently moving the cable.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the cable with a known-good compatible accessory and verified a stable signal during normal positioning and movement.

helpfulDetails: Whether signal was noisy, intermittent, or absent

title: Canon Alphenix Sky+ Angiography System - System Freezes, Restarts, or Loses Communication
description: Troubleshoot intermittent freezes, unexpected restarts, subsystem dropouts, or communication loss caused by connections, power, environment, peripherals, or service-level faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Procedure
steps.instructions: If the system freezes, restarts, or loses communication during patient care, stop relying on it immediately. Coordinate a safe procedure pause or alternate clinical workflow as appropriate. Expected outcome: Patient care no longer depends on an unstable angiography system.

steps.title: 2. Characterize the Event
steps.instructions: Determine what froze or restarted, which components remained operational, whether communication returned automatically, and what was happening immediately before the event. Record all displayed messages and timestamps. Expected outcome: The event is described precisely enough to distinguish a whole-system restart from an isolated subsystem or communication loss.

steps.title: 3. Check for Power Disturbance
steps.instructions: Verify facility power status and inspect accessible power connections. Determine whether other room equipment experienced a simultaneous interruption. Expected outcome: An obvious external power disturbance is identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Interconnects
steps.instructions: Check accessible network, display, console, control, detector-interface, and other external system connections for looseness, damage, strain, or movement-related interruption. Expected outcome: All external communication paths are securely connected.

steps.title: 5. Check Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Look for blocked ventilation, excessive dust at accessible vents, nearby heat sources, liquid exposure, unusual room conditions, or evidence that equipment is overheating. Do not open covers to inspect internal cooling components. Expected outcome: No correctable external environmental condition is contributing to instability.

steps.title: 6. Check External Peripherals and Accessories
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue began after connecting or changing an external accessory, peripheral, network device, or removable media. Disconnect only nonessential approved peripherals when safe and appropriate to isolate the condition. Expected outcome: A problematic external peripheral is identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: After patient care is protected, use the normal approved shutdown and restart process. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a system displaying signs of overheating, electrical damage, smoke, or unusual odor. Expected outcome: The system completes startup and all expected subsystems reconnect.

steps.title: 8. Observe System Stability
steps.instructions: Allow the system to operate through representative non-patient functions and normal equipment positioning. Watch for renewed freezing, communication loss, or unexpected restart. Expected outcome: The system remains stable without recurring interruption.

steps.title: 9. Verify Communication and Major Functions
steps.instructions: Confirm operator displays, controls, system components, and required network or subsystem communication paths are restored. Perform applicable return-to-service testing. Expected outcome: The system remains fully responsive and connected. If the event was caused by an identified external condition and does not recur, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Any Recurrent Instability
steps.instructions: If the freeze, restart, or communication loss repeats or no external cause is confirmed, remove the system from service. Expected outcome: An intermittently unstable angiography system is not returned to patient use without further evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Canon Alphenix Sky+ intermittently lost communication with an operator display during system positioning.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external display communication cable loose enough to interrupt communication when the connected equipment moved.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, exercised the system through normal positioning, verified stable display communication and system operation, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact component that froze or restarted

title: Canon Alphenix Sky+ Angiography System - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Troubleshoot startup failure, incomplete initialization, power loss, external power problems, emergency-stop conditions, disconnected components, or system communication problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unavailable or unreliable angiography system while it is needed for an active procedure. If a patient is involved, coordinate with clinical staff and move care to an appropriate alternative system or workflow before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The patient is no longer dependent on the affected system and troubleshooting can proceed safely.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the entire system is unpowered, some components power on, startup stops at a particular stage, or an error message appears. Record the exact message and which consoles, displays, generators, tables, or related components appear operational. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to a complete power loss, partial-system problem, or startup/communication failure.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility Power
steps.instructions: Confirm that the system's normal facility power source is available. Check accessible disconnects, approved power controls, and room power indicators for an abnormal condition. Do not reset breakers or facility electrical protection unless authorized by site procedure. Expected outcome: Required facility power is available. If restoring an approved external power condition returns the system to normal startup, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Power and Communication Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible power cords, interconnect cables, console connections, display connections, and external system cables for looseness, physical damage, strain, or accidental disconnection. Expected outcome: All accessible connections are secure and undamaged. Correcting a loose external connection restores normal startup if it was the cause.

steps.title: 5. Check Emergency and Safety Controls
steps.instructions: Verify that accessible emergency-stop or shutdown controls have not been activated and that no room safety condition is intentionally preventing operation. Do not bypass or defeat a safety interlock. Expected outcome: No external safety control is preventing startup. If an unintentionally activated control is safely restored and startup completes normally, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Check Connected System Components
steps.instructions: Verify that required external consoles, monitors, operator controls, table interfaces, imaging components, and approved peripherals are connected and powered as applicable. Look for one subsystem that remains offline while the rest of the system starts. Expected outcome: Required system components are present and available for initialization.

steps.title: 7. Perform an Approved Restart
steps.instructions: If patient care is protected and no hardware damage, smoke, odor, overheating, or electrical abnormality is present, perform a normal shutdown and restart using approved operating controls. Expected outcome: The system completes startup without repeating the reported failure. If it does, proceed to final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm that the system reaches its normal ready condition and that operator controls, displays, table functions, communications, and required imaging readiness indicators behave normally. Complete any required return-to-service testing applicable to the work performed. Expected outcome: The angiography system starts reliably and passes applicable functional checks.

steps.title: 9. Escalate an Unresolved Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If startup repeatedly fails, a subsystem remains unavailable, or normal operation cannot be verified, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The system remains removed from clinical use and is referred for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Canon Alphenix Sky+ stopped during startup and would not reach the ready condition.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an accessible external system interconnect cable partially disconnected.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, restarted the system, verified normal startup and basic system operation, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Components that powered on or remained off
Condition of external cables and connections
Any unusual sound, heat, odor, or visible damage

title: Canon Alphenix Sky+ Angiography System - Therapy or Output Will Not Start
description: Troubleshoot commanded system output that will not initiate because of readiness, controls, accessories, interlocks, configuration, or system communication problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop the Procedure if Needed
steps.instructions: If required imaging or system output cannot be initiated reliably, do not continue an invasive procedure unless the clinical team has established a safe alternative plan. Expected outcome: Patient care is not dependent on an angiography system that cannot reliably produce the required output.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Output Failure
steps.instructions: Determine which commanded function will not start, whether the request is ignored or inhibited, and whether the system displays a readiness message, warning, or other status indication. Expected outcome: The failure is defined as a specific output/readiness problem rather than a general system complaint.

steps.title: 3. Verify Overall System Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm that the system has completed startup and is not displaying an unresolved fault or unavailable subsystem. Verify that required system components appear online. Expected outcome: The system reaches the normal state required before initiating output.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Controls and Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible hand controls, foot controls, switches, cables, connectors, and operator interfaces associated with the requested function. Check for obvious damage or loose connections. Expected outcome: External command devices are connected, undamaged, and responsive.

steps.title: 5. Check Safety Interlocks and Positioning
steps.instructions: Verify that applicable table, gantry, detector, room safety, collision-prevention, or other normal safety conditions are satisfied. Never bypass a safety interlock to obtain output. Expected outcome: No legitimate external safety condition is intentionally inhibiting operation.

steps.title: 6. Verify Accessories and Required Modules
steps.instructions: Confirm that required approved accessories or modules are attached and recognized where the requested function depends on them. Expected outcome: All required external components are present and recognized.

steps.title: 7. Verify Accessible Operating Selections
steps.instructions: Check normal user-accessible mode and function selections to confirm that the requested operation is enabled and appropriate for the current setup. Do not alter restricted service configuration. Expected outcome: The requested function is correctly selected and available.

steps.title: 8. Test With Known-Good External Controls When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If an approved interchangeable external control or accessory is available, substitute it to determine whether the failure follows the accessory. Expected outcome: A known-good substitute restores normal activation if the external control was defective.

steps.title: 9. Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting an external cause, verify the requested output using an appropriate non-patient functional test and any required safety checks before clinical use. Expected outcome: Output starts reliably when commanded and terminates normally. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Output Failure
steps.instructions: If output remains inhibited despite correct readiness, connections, accessories, positioning, and controls, remove the system from service. Expected outcome: Unreliable output is not used clinically and the system is referred for qualified service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Canon Alphenix Sky+ would not initiate the requested imaging output when commanded.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external foot control connection partially seated and confirmed normal control recognition after reseating it.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, verified reliable activation with a non-patient functional check, and returned the system to service.

helpfulDetails: Function or output that would not start

title: Canon Aplio i900 CV Echocardiography System - Accessory or Module Is Not Recognized
description: Troubleshooting an attached probe, accessory, peripheral, or module that is missing, unavailable, intermittently detected, or not accepted by the system.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Imaging Capability
steps.instructions: If the unrecognized accessory is required for the current examination, stop using that accessory and move to another compatible verified accessory or another echocardiography system. Do not repeatedly connect and disconnect patient-applied equipment during active patient dependence. Expected outcome: Patient care continues using verified equipment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Recognition Problem
steps.instructions: Identify which probe, accessory, module, or peripheral is not recognized and whether the issue occurs consistently. Record any on-screen message exactly. Determine whether other accessories of the same general type are recognized normally. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to one accessory, one connection position, or the system generally.

steps.title: 3. Verify Compatibility and Intended Connection
steps.instructions: Confirm that the accessory is intended for use with the Aplio i900 CV and is connected to the correct accessible interface according to approved documentation. Do not force a connector that does not seat normally. Expected outcome: The correct accessory and connection point are being used.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Accessory and Connector Externally
steps.instructions: Disconnect the accessory when safe and inspect the accessible connector, cable, strain relief, latch, contacts, and housing for contamination, bent or damaged areas, fluid intrusion, or physical damage. Inspect the system-side connection without inserting tools or altering contacts. Expected outcome: The accessory and connection are clean, dry, intact, and capable of seating securely.

steps.title: 5. Reconnect the Accessory Correctly
steps.instructions: Reconnect the accessory fully using its normal locking or seating mechanism. Do not apply excessive force. Observe whether the system recognizes it after proper connection. Expected outcome: The accessory is recognized and becomes available. If recognition is stable, proceed to functional verification.

steps.title: 6. Try Another Approved Connection Position When Applicable
steps.instructions: If the system provides another compatible external connection position and normal workflow permits it, test the accessory there. This helps distinguish an accessory problem from a single connection-path problem. Expected outcome: Recognition at another compatible connection point helps isolate the issue to the accessory or original connection location.

steps.title: 7. Use a Known-Good Compatible Accessory
steps.instructions: When available, connect a known-good compatible accessory of the same appropriate type. Do not substitute equipment that has not been approved for the system. Expected outcome: If the known-good accessory is recognized, the original accessory is suspect. If neither is recognized, a system-side problem becomes more likely.

steps.title: 8. Restart the System if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If external inspection and substitution do not resolve the problem and there is no sign of connector damage, perform a normal system restart. Reconnect or recheck the accessory according to normal workflow. Expected outcome: The system completes startup and recognizes the accessory normally.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify that the recognized accessory operates correctly during an appropriate functional test. For imaging probes or clinically significant modules, verify expected image acquisition or functional behavior before clinical use. Expected outcome: Recognition remains stable and the accessory functions normally. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Recognition Failures
steps.instructions: If known-good compatible accessories are not recognized, a connection point is physically damaged, or recognition remains intermittent, remove the affected accessory or system from service as appropriate. Do not perform internal connector or board-level repair. Expected outcome: The unresolved problem is contained and referred for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that a probe connected to the Aplio i900 CV was not consistently recognized by the system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the probe connector was not fully seated and locked into the system connection.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reconnected the probe correctly, verified stable recognition and image acquisition, and returned the system to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether another compatible connection was tested

title: Canon Aplio i900 CV Echocardiography System - Alarm Persists or Audio Is Weak or Missing
description: Troubleshooting persistent system alerts or weak, distorted, intermittent, or absent audible output caused by settings, obstruction, connection, or system-level problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Do Not Depend on Unreliable Audible Indications
steps.instructions: If an audible indication needed for safe workflow cannot be heard or a persistent alert prevents normal operation, stop relying on the affected system until the condition is understood. Use another verified system when necessary. Expected outcome: Clinical workflow does not depend on unreliable system audio or unresolved alert behavior.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Alert or Audio Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether an alert will not clear, audio is absent, sound is unusually weak, audio is distorted, or the system repeatedly produces an unexpected audible indication. Record any corresponding on-screen message exactly. Expected outcome: The complaint is separated into alert-condition, audio-output, or broader system behavior.

steps.title: 3. Address the Displayed Condition First
steps.instructions: If an alert corresponds to a visible system condition, inspect the external cause indicated by the normal user interface. Do not silence or bypass a persistent warning without resolving its cause. Expected outcome: A legitimate external condition is corrected and the alert clears normally, or the problem remains for further isolation.

steps.title: 4. Verify Accessible Audio Settings
steps.instructions: Check user-accessible sound or volume settings relevant to the reported function. Compare them with normal clinical settings if available. Do not enter restricted menus or change protected alarm configuration. Expected outcome: Audio settings are appropriate and have not been unintentionally reduced or disabled.

steps.title: 5. Inspect for Physical Obstruction or Damage
steps.instructions: Check accessible speaker areas and the console for tape, covers, drapes, cleaning material, liquid contamination, or physical damage that could interfere with audible output. Expected outcome: Audio openings are unobstructed and no obvious external damage is present.

steps.title: 6. Check External Audio Connections When Applicable
steps.instructions: If external audio equipment is being used, inspect the accessible cable and connection and remove the external device temporarily if appropriate. Determine whether normal system audio returns. Expected outcome: External audio accessories are ruled in or out as the cause.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: If no external cause is found, complete a normal shutdown and restart. Observe whether the persistent alert returns and whether system audio is restored. Expected outcome: Normal audio operation returns and no unexplained alert persists.

steps.title: 8. Verify Audio and System Operation
steps.instructions: Use normal approved system functions to confirm that audible output can be heard clearly and that expected visual indications are also present where applicable. Verify that no unresolved warning remains. Expected outcome: Audio is clearly functional and the system is free of unexplained persistent alerts. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Unresolved Audio or Alert Problems
steps.instructions: If audio remains absent or unreliable, or an unexplained alert persists after external causes have been ruled out, remove the system from service when the condition affects safe clinical operation. Do not repair speakers, internal amplifiers, boards, or protected alarm circuitry at the external troubleshooting level. Expected outcome: A probable internal audio, control, software, or system-status problem is referred for qualified repair.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that audible system feedback from the Aplio i900 CV was difficult to hear during examinations.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the user-accessible audio level had been reduced from its normal department setting.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering restored the appropriate audio setting, verified clear audible output and normal system operation, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the alert was persistent or intermittent

title: Canon Aplio i900 CV Echocardiography System - Battery Will Not Charge or Runtime Is Short
description: Troubleshooting battery charging or reduced runtime caused by AC power, connection, battery condition, charging state, workload, or service-level problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Clinical Coverage
steps.instructions: Do not depend on an unreliable battery for an examination where unexpected shutdown could interrupt clinically necessary imaging or data handling. Connect the system to verified AC power or move the examination to another verified system. Expected outcome: Clinical imaging does not depend on uncertain battery operation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the battery does not indicate charging, charges incompletely, discharges unusually quickly, or cannot maintain the system during expected battery-supported operation. Record the displayed battery status and when the behavior occurs. Expected outcome: The complaint is identified as a charging, capacity, indication, or runtime problem.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power Is Actually Available
steps.instructions: Confirm that the system is connected to a verified working receptacle and that the external power cord and accessible connections are secure and undamaged. A battery cannot charge normally if facility AC is absent or intermittent. Expected outcome: Reliable AC power is confirmed. If restoring AC power restores normal charging, continue through verification and stop troubleshooting when normal operation is confirmed.

steps.title: 4. Observe the Battery and Charging Indications
steps.instructions: With the system connected to verified AC power, observe the normal battery or charging indications available on the system. Record any warning or abnormal indication exactly as shown. Do not infer battery failure solely from runtime complaints. Expected outcome: The system recognizes the available power source and displays an appropriate charging or battery state.

steps.title: 5. Allow Normal Charging Opportunity
steps.instructions: If the system has been stored, transported, or heavily used on battery, allow it to remain connected to AC power under normal approved conditions. Avoid making conclusions from a battery that has not had a reasonable opportunity to charge. Expected outcome: Battery state improves while connected to AC power and subsequently supports normal operation.

steps.title: 6. Check for External Conditions Affecting Runtime
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint occurred during unusually long mobile use, repeated startups, extended operation away from AC, or after prolonged storage. Inspect accessible battery-related areas for obvious swelling, leakage, heat, or damage without opening the battery or internal compartments beyond authorized access. Expected outcome: No unsafe physical battery condition is present, and usage conditions are understood.

steps.title: 7. Compare Behavior on AC and Battery Operation
steps.instructions: When safe and appropriate, verify stable operation on AC and then observe the system during approved battery-supported operation. Do not conduct extended discharge testing on a device needed for clinical care. Expected outcome: The system remains stable and the battery status behaves normally. If charging and runtime return to normal, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify normal startup, charging indication, stable operation, and any applicable battery-related checks required by facility policy or Canon documentation. Confirm that no battery warning persists. Expected outcome: Battery-supported operation and charging are acceptable for return to clinical service.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Battery Problems
steps.instructions: If verified AC power is available but charging remains abnormal, runtime remains significantly degraded, or the battery shows physical damage or abnormal heat, remove the system from battery-dependent service. Do not attempt cell-level repair or internal charging-circuit troubleshooting. Expected outcome: A suspected battery, charging, power-management, or internal service-level problem is safely referred for repair.
