CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the system was connected to a receptacle that was not supplying AC power.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering connected the system to a verified powered receptacle, confirmed normal charging indication and stable operation, and returned the unit to service.

title: Canon Aplio i900 CV Echocardiography System - Display, Touchscreen, or Controls Are Unresponsive
description: Troubleshooting blank, frozen, intermittent, or unresponsive user-interface components caused by power, connection, obstruction, contamination, accessory, or system-level problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Dependence on Unreliable Controls
steps.instructions: If the display, touchscreen, or controls cannot be trusted during a patient examination, stop using the system for clinical imaging and transition to another verified unit as needed. Do not continue an examination if critical information cannot be viewed or controls cannot be operated reliably. Expected outcome: Patient care no longer depends on an unreliable interface.

steps.title: 2. Identify Exactly What Is Unresponsive
steps.instructions: Determine whether the entire system is frozen, only one display is blank, the touchscreen does not respond, a limited group of controls is affected, or controls respond intermittently. Confirm whether imaging continues behind the interface problem. Expected outcome: The issue is narrowed to a specific interface component or a broader system freeze.

steps.title: 3. Check System Power and Startup State
steps.instructions: Verify that the system is fully powered and has completed normal startup. A blank or inactive display during incomplete startup can be mistaken for an isolated display failure. Record any message or abnormal indicator. Expected outcome: The system is confirmed to be fully started, or the problem is redirected to a startup issue.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Display and Control Surfaces
steps.instructions: Check for liquid, gel, cleaning residue, adhesive, protective material, physical obstruction, or visible damage affecting the touchscreen or controls. Clean only using approved methods and materials. Confirm that nothing is continuously pressing against controls. Expected outcome: Control surfaces are clean, dry, unobstructed, and undamaged. If removing contamination or obstruction restores normal response, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Check Accessible Positioning and External Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible display or console areas for evidence that movement or repositioning has placed tension on visible cables or connectors. Verify only externally accessible connections intended for routine service or user access. Do not disassemble display housings or internal control panels. Expected outcome: No external connection or mechanical positioning issue is causing the problem.

steps.title: 6. Disconnect Nonessential External Peripherals
steps.instructions: When appropriate, disconnect nonessential USB devices or externally attached peripherals that could interfere with normal system operation. Recheck the interface. Expected outcome: The interface operates normally without a problematic peripheral. If so, isolate the external device before returning the system to use.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled System Restart
steps.instructions: If the controls permit normal shutdown, shut down and restart the system using the normal process. Avoid forced or repeated power cycling unless required by approved service guidance. Expected outcome: The system restarts with responsive displays and controls. If responsiveness remains stable, proceed to verification.

steps.title: 8. Verify Clinical Interface Functions
steps.instructions: Check the display, touchscreen, keyboard or control panel functions used for normal echocardiography operation. Verify basic image acquisition and confirm that interface response remains stable. Expected outcome: Required controls respond consistently and the system is suitable for clinical use. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Recurrent or Persistent Unresponsiveness
steps.instructions: If the interface remains blank, frozen, intermittent, or partially unresponsive after external checks and a controlled restart, remove the system from service. Do not perform internal display, control-board, computer, or wiring repair without proper authorization. Expected outcome: A probable internal hardware, software, or communication problem is appropriately escalated.

CCR.Complaint: Sonography staff reported that touchscreen selections on the Canon Aplio i900 CV were intermittently unresponsive.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried ultrasound gel contamination along the touchscreen surface causing unreliable touch response.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned the surface using the approved method, verified consistent touchscreen and control operation, completed functional testing, and returned the system to service.

Whether the problem was constant or intermittent

title: Canon Aplio i900 CV Echocardiography System - Network, Data Export, or Interface Communication Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed network connectivity, study transfer, data export, or interface communication caused by cabling, destination availability, configuration, media, or infrastructure problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Study Data
steps.instructions: Do not interrupt an active patient examination solely to troubleshoot network connectivity unless required for safety. Preserve locally available patient data and prevent duplicate, incomplete, or misassociated records. Use an approved alternate workflow if immediate data transfer is clinically necessary. Expected outcome: Patient imaging and study data are protected while communication troubleshooting occurs.

steps.title: 2. Define the Exact Communication Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the system has no network connection, cannot reach a destination, cannot send a study, cannot export to approved media, or cannot communicate with an external interface. Record any error message exactly and identify whether the issue affects all destinations or only one. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to the local system, one destination, one interface, or the broader network.

steps.title: 3. Check the Physical Network Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect the accessible network cable and connector for looseness, damage, bent locking tabs, or disconnection. Verify that the cable is connected to the intended network connection. Check normal external link indications when available. Expected outcome: The physical network connection is secure and shows expected connectivity.

steps.title: 4. Test With a Known-Good Network Connection When Permitted
steps.instructions: If facility policy allows, substitute a known-good network cable or test the approved wall connection using appropriate methods. Coordinate with IT when network infrastructure testing is required. Expected outcome: A faulty cable or local network connection is identified, or the physical path is ruled out.

steps.title: 5. Determine the Scope of the Outage
steps.instructions: Check whether other imaging systems or workstations are experiencing similar communication problems with the same destination. Confirm destination availability with the responsible clinical or IT team when necessary. Expected outcome: The issue is identified as device-specific or infrastructure/destination-related.

steps.title: 6. Verify User-Accessible Network and Destination Information
steps.instructions: Review the system's accessible communication status and approved configuration information without making unauthorized changes. Compare settings with documented values or a known working configuration. Do not guess addresses, ports, destination parameters, or patient-data mappings. Expected outcome: No obvious configuration discrepancy is found, or an authorized configuration issue is identified for correction.

steps.title: 7. Check Data Export Media or Peripheral When Applicable
steps.instructions: For export failures, verify that the approved media or connected peripheral is compatible, properly connected, recognized, and has appropriate available capacity. Test with another approved known-good device when possible. Expected outcome: The export accessory is either confirmed functional or identified as the source of failure.

steps.title: 8. Retry a Controlled Test Transfer
steps.instructions: After correcting any external connection or infrastructure issue, perform an approved test transfer or export using nonclinical test data or another facility-approved method. Confirm receipt at the intended destination rather than relying solely on the local send status. Expected outcome: Data reaches the intended destination completely and correctly.

steps.title: 9. Verify the Complete Clinical Communication Path
steps.instructions: Where patient studies are involved, confirm the study appears at the correct receiving system and is associated appropriately. Ensure queued or failed transfers are addressed according to department workflow. Expected outcome: End-to-end communication is restored. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Communication Failure
steps.instructions: If physical connections, destination availability, external media, and documented accessible settings are correct but communication still fails, escalate to qualified Canon service, IT, PACS/interface support, or the responsible infrastructure team. Expected outcome: A probable software, configuration, network-infrastructure, interface, or internal communication problem is assigned to the appropriate support group.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Aplio i900 CV could not transfer completed studies to the normal receiving destination.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external network cable was not fully seated at the system connection.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the network cable, completed an approved test transfer, confirmed successful receipt at the destination, and returned the system to normal service.

helpfulDetails: Whether all or one destination was affected
Wall connection or cable test result

title: Canon Aplio i900 CV Echocardiography System - Output Is Low, Unstable, or Inaccurate
description: Troubleshooting weak, unstable, or inaccurate imaging-related output caused by probe condition, connections, settings, positioning, patient interface, or system-level problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Do Not Rely on Questionable Imaging Performance
steps.instructions: If the displayed imaging information appears unreliable or inconsistent with the clinical situation, do not continue making clinical decisions from the affected system. Move the examination to another verified echocardiography system or probe as appropriate. Expected outcome: Patient assessment does not depend on questionable system performance.

steps.title: 2. Confirm What Is Low, Unstable, or Inaccurate
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves image brightness, signal strength, Doppler-related information, measurement behavior, intermittent image loss, or another observable imaging output. Identify the probe and examination conditions involved. Expected outcome: The complaint is defined well enough to reproduce and isolate safely.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Probe and Cable Externally
steps.instructions: Examine the probe housing, acoustic surface, cable, strain relief, connector, and accessible contacts for cracks, cuts, contamination, liquid intrusion, bent areas, or other damage. Remove a visibly damaged probe from service. Expected outcome: The probe is externally intact and suitable for further testing.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Probe Connection
steps.instructions: Confirm the probe is fully seated and recognized by the system. Reseat it using the normal connection method if appropriate. Check whether the symptom changes when the cable is positioned normally without pulling or flexing it excessively. Expected outcome: The connection is secure and the output remains stable during normal cable positioning.

steps.title: 5. Check Patient Interface and Probe Positioning
steps.instructions: Confirm appropriate acoustic coupling, correct probe positioning, and adequate approved ultrasound gel. Rule out poor contact or technique-related effects before assuming equipment failure. Expected outcome: The image improves when proper coupling and positioning are established, or the equipment-related symptom remains reproducible.

steps.title: 6. Review User-Accessible Imaging Settings
steps.instructions: Verify that relevant imaging mode and adjustable settings have not been unintentionally changed. Compare with a known normal setup or facility-approved baseline when available. Do not alter protected calibration or service parameters. Expected outcome: The system is operating with appropriate user-accessible settings for the test being performed.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Compatible Probe
steps.instructions: When available, use a known-good compatible probe under comparable test conditions. If the symptom follows the original probe, remove that probe from service. If the issue occurs with multiple known-good probes, the system becomes more suspect. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to the probe or remains associated with the system.

steps.title: 8. Check the Operating Environment
steps.instructions: Look for nearby equipment, damaged power accessories, unusual electrical interference, or room conditions associated with the complaint. If the issue occurs only in one room or location, compare operation in another suitable location when practical. Expected outcome: Environmental or infrastructure influence is either identified or reasonably ruled out.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting an external cause, verify stable image acquisition and the affected imaging function using an appropriate approved test method. If measurement accuracy is part of the complaint, use appropriate approved test equipment or procedures rather than visual judgment alone. Expected outcome: Imaging output is stable and appropriate functional verification passes. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Unresolved Performance Problems
steps.instructions: If poor or inaccurate output persists with a known-good probe, correct settings, proper test conditions, and no obvious environmental cause, remove the system from service. Do not attempt internal imaging-board, transmitter, receiver, or signal-path repair. Expected outcome: A suspected internal imaging, calibration, software, or signal-processing problem is referred for qualified service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported weak and intermittently degraded cardiac images when using one probe on the Aplio i900 CV.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found visible damage to the affected probe cable, while a known-good compatible probe produced stable images.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the damaged probe from service, verified stable imaging with the known-good probe, and returned the system to service with the affected accessory excluded.

Whether the issue followed the probe or system

title: Canon Aplio i900 CV Echocardiography System - Preventive Maintenance or Electrical Safety Test Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed PM or electrical safety testing caused by setup, accessories, power cords, grounding, test equipment, physical damage, or service-level problems.

steps.title: 1. Remove Failed Equipment From Clinical Availability
steps.instructions: Do not return the Aplio i900 CV to patient use after a failed required preventive-maintenance or electrical safety test until the failure is understood and corrected. Clearly control the device's status during evaluation. Expected outcome: Equipment that has not met required verification remains unavailable for clinical use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Test That Failed
steps.instructions: Identify the PM inspection, functional check, or electrical safety measurement that did not meet the applicable requirement. Record the actual observed result and the requirement being applied from facility policy, manufacturer documentation, or the approved test procedure. Do not invent or substitute limits. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly defined and based on the correct approved requirement.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Test Setup and Test Equipment
steps.instructions: Confirm that the approved test instrument is within its required calibration status, correctly configured, and connected according to the applicable procedure. Inspect test leads and adapters for damage or poor connection. Expected outcome: The failed result is not caused by incorrect test setup or defective test accessories.

steps.title: 4. Perform a Complete External Inspection
steps.instructions: Inspect the system, power cord, plug, strain relief, accessible connectors, wheels or mechanical components, probe cables, and other applicable external parts for damage, contamination, missing hardware, or evidence of liquid intrusion. Expected outcome: External physical defects are identified before further electrical or functional testing.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Facility Power Source
steps.instructions: When the failure could be influenced by the AC supply or grounding path, verify the test receptacle using approved equipment and facility procedures. Do not condemn the system based on measurements taken from an unverified source. Expected outcome: The electrical source used for testing is suitable for the approved procedure.

steps.title: 6. Check the Power Cord and Accessible Grounding Path
steps.instructions: Inspect the equipment power cord and plug carefully. If the approved procedure permits, evaluate the cord and accessible protective grounding path using the appropriate test equipment. Replace only components authorized for field replacement. Expected outcome: An external cord or connection problem is identified and corrected, or the external grounding path is ruled out.

steps.title: 7. Remove Nonessential External Accessories and Retest When Appropriate
steps.instructions: An externally connected accessory can affect some test results. Follow the approved PM or electrical safety procedure regarding which accessories should be connected. Retest using the required configuration rather than arbitrarily disconnecting components. Expected outcome: The result is confirmed under the correct test configuration.

steps.title: 8. Verify Functional PM Items Separately
steps.instructions: If the failure concerns a functional PM item rather than electrical safety, inspect the relevant probe, control, display, connection, mobility feature, or external accessory and test it according to approved procedures. Keep inspection, testing, calibration, and repair distinct in the work documentation. Expected outcome: A correctable external defect is identified or the failure remains reproducible.

steps.title: 9. Repeat the Failed Test After Correction
steps.instructions: After correcting a verified external cause, repeat the exact failed test using the approved procedure and test equipment. Do not consider the device repaired solely because the visible defect was corrected. Expected outcome: The previously failed test now meets the applicable documented requirement. If all remaining PM checks also pass, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Any Persistent Safety or PM Failure
steps.instructions: If the test continues to fail after setup, source, cord, accessory, and external conditions have been verified, stop troubleshooting at the authorized level. Do not adjust internal power, grounding, leakage, calibration, or circuit components merely to obtain a passing result. Expected outcome: A suspected internal electrical, mechanical, calibration, or functional problem is referred for qualified service.

steps.title: 11. Complete Return-to-Service Testing and Documentation
steps.instructions: After repair, repeat the required failed test and complete all applicable PM, functional, and electrical safety checks required by facility policy before releasing the system. Record actual results according to department procedures. Expected outcome: The Aplio i900 CV meets all applicable return-to-service requirements and its status is documented correctly.

CCR.Complaint: The Canon Aplio i900 CV failed an electrical safety check during scheduled preventive maintenance.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found physical damage to the detachable external power cord that affected the required electrical safety verification.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the damaged cord with an approved replacement, repeated the electrical safety and applicable functional tests successfully, documented the results, and returned the system to service.

Test equipment identification and calibration status
Final PM and electrical safety status

title: Canon Aplio i900 CV Echocardiography System - Self-Test or Calibration Will Not Complete
description: Troubleshooting incomplete self-test or calibration caused by startup state, connected accessories, setup conditions, external interference, configuration, or service-level problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the System From Clinical Dependence
steps.instructions: Do not use the Aplio i900 CV for patient imaging when a required self-test or calibration has failed and system performance cannot be verified. Move the examination to another verified system. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on unverified equipment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Test Is Failing
steps.instructions: Identify whether the problem occurs during startup self-test, a user-accessible calibration, or another approved verification process. Record the exact displayed message, stage, and circumstances of the failure. Do not enter restricted service menus. Expected outcome: The failed process and repeatable symptom are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Normal Startup and Stable Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the system starts normally and is connected to a verified AC source. An unstable power source or incomplete startup can prevent tests from completing reliably. Expected outcome: Stable power and normal system readiness are confirmed.

steps.title: 4. Check Required External Accessories and Connections
steps.instructions: Verify that any accessory, probe, cable, or approved test item required for the particular procedure is present, compatible, correctly connected, and undamaged. Remove unrelated accessories if appropriate. Expected outcome: The test has the correct external setup and no obvious connection problem.

steps.title: 5. Inspect for Contamination or Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Check relevant accessible connectors, probe surfaces, cables, accessories, and external interfaces for gel, liquid, debris, bent areas, damage, or poor seating. Correct only external issues within Clinical Engineering scope. Expected outcome: External components required for testing are clean, intact, and properly connected.

steps.title: 6. Verify Applicable Settings and Test Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm that the system is in the proper normal operating state for the approved self-test or calibration being performed. Verify relevant user-accessible settings against approved documentation. Do not change protected configuration simply to make a test pass. Expected outcome: The test is being performed under the correct supported conditions.

steps.title: 7. Use a Known-Good Compatible Accessory When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the failing test depends on a probe or external accessory, substitute a known-good compatible item when available. Repeat only the approved test. Expected outcome: A successful test with the known-good accessory isolates the original accessory as the likely cause.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Restart and Repeat Once
steps.instructions: If no external cause is found, perform a normal shutdown and restart. Repeat the test under the same correct conditions. Avoid repeated test cycling when the same failure consistently returns. Expected outcome: The self-test or calibration completes normally. If it does, proceed to functional verification.

steps.title: 9. Verify Normal Imaging Function
steps.instructions: After a successful test, verify basic imaging operation and any functions related to the failed process. Complete return-to-service testing required by policy. Expected outcome: The test passes and the system performs normally. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate a Repeatable Test Failure
steps.instructions: If the same self-test or calibration failure remains after external setup, accessory, power, and restart checks, stop troubleshooting at the external level. Do not bypass the failure or alter unauthorized calibration data. Expected outcome: An unresolved calibration, software, hardware, or internal communication issue is referred for qualified service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Aplio i900 CV would not complete an expected system verification after a probe was connected.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found contamination on the accessible probe connector that prevented a reliable connection.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned and reconnected the probe using the approved method, repeated the verification successfully, confirmed basic imaging operation, and returned the system to service.

title: Canon Aplio i900 CV Echocardiography System - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Troubleshooting a system that remains off, loses power during startup, or cannot reach normal operating readiness because of external power or connection problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Clinical Coverage
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot the Aplio i900 CV while it is required for active patient imaging. Move the examination to another verified echocardiography system when clinical imaging cannot be delayed. If there is smoke, unusual odor, excessive heat, liquid intrusion, visible electrical damage, or evidence of arcing, disconnect the system from AC power when safe and remove it from service immediately. Expected outcome: Patient care is transferred safely and the system can be evaluated without affecting an active examination.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Attempt normal startup while observing the system. Determine whether there are no signs of power, whether indicators illuminate without completing startup, whether the display remains blank, or whether startup repeatedly stops or restarts. Record any visible message exactly as displayed. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to no power, incomplete startup, display-related behavior, or repeated interruption.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Confirm that the system is connected securely to an appropriate facility receptacle. Inspect the accessible plug and power cord for looseness, damaged insulation, bent contacts, heat damage, or contamination. Verify the receptacle with approved test equipment or another method permitted by facility policy. Avoid relying solely on another device appearing to work from the same area. Expected outcome: A reliable AC source and intact external power connection are confirmed. If correcting the outlet or power connection restores normal startup, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Accessible Power Connections and Controls
steps.instructions: Verify that accessible system power connections are fully seated and that the normal power control operates freely. Inspect for a partially connected cord caused by transport, cleaning, or repositioning. Do not open covers or access internal power assemblies. Expected outcome: External power connections and controls are secure and undamaged.

steps.title: 5. Remove Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external USB devices, network peripherals, removable accessories, and other externally connected equipment when doing so is safe and permitted. Leave only the equipment required for normal system startup. Attempt startup again. Expected outcome: The system starts normally without an external accessory preventing initialization. If it does, isolate the accessory before returning the system to service.

steps.title: 6. Check for Environmental or Transport-Related Causes
steps.instructions: Confirm that the system is not positioned against a wall, drape, storage item, or other obstruction that could interfere with ventilation. Check for recent transport, liquid exposure, extreme room conditions, or physical impact that may have preceded the problem. Expected outcome: No obvious environmental or physical condition is preventing normal startup.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Restart When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the system has partial power but does not complete startup, perform only the normal shutdown/restart process available to the operator or Clinical Engineering. Do not repeatedly cycle power if abnormal noises, overheating, odor, or electrical symptoms are present. Expected outcome: The Aplio i900 CV completes startup and reaches its normal ready state. If startup completes normally and remains stable, proceed to functional verification.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After successful startup, verify that the display, controls, probe recognition, basic imaging operation, and other functions necessary for clinical use operate normally. Confirm no startup warning remains. Complete any required return-to-service checks according to facility policy and approved Canon documentation. Expected outcome: The system remains powered, reaches normal operating readiness, and passes applicable functional checks. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate an Unresolved Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If verified AC power is present and external causes have been ruled out but the system remains dead, stalls during startup, or repeatedly restarts, stop external troubleshooting. Do not proceed into internal power supplies, computer assemblies, or board-level diagnostics unless specifically authorized and trained. Expected outcome: An unresolved system-level failure is appropriately contained and referred for qualified service.

CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the AC power cord partially disengaged at the system connection after the unit had been repositioned.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the power connection, restarted the system, verified normal startup and basic imaging operation, and returned the unit to service.

title: Canon Aplio i900 CV Echocardiography System - Unexpected Shutdown, Freeze, or Restart
description: Troubleshooting intermittent shutdowns, freezes, or restarts caused by power, peripherals, environment, workload, connections, or internal hardware and software problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Clinical Continuity
steps.instructions: If the Aplio i900 CV freezes, shuts down, or restarts during an examination, stop depending on it for patient imaging. Move the examination to another verified system when necessary and preserve recoverable study data according to department workflow. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without dependence on an unstable system.

steps.title: 2. Document the Exact Failure Pattern
steps.instructions: Determine whether the system powered off completely, froze with the display still active, restarted automatically, or became unresponsive after a specific action. Record what the system was doing immediately before the event and any displayed message. Expected outcome: The symptom is characterized well enough to distinguish power interruption from software or system instability.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility AC Power
steps.instructions: Inspect the external power cord, plug, and accessible system connection. Confirm the receptacle is reliable using approved methods. Determine whether the system was operating from AC or battery when the event occurred. Expected outcome: External power loss or a loose connection is corrected or ruled out.

steps.title: 4. Inspect for Physical and Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Check for blocked ventilation, excessive external heat, liquid contamination, recent impact, cable tension, or positioning that could affect system operation. Do not obstruct cooling areas during testing. Expected outcome: The system is appropriately positioned with no obvious external environmental cause.

steps.title: 5. Disconnect Nonessential Peripherals
steps.instructions: When appropriate, disconnect nonessential USB devices, external storage, network peripherals, or other removable accessories. Operate the system under controlled conditions to determine whether instability returns. Expected outcome: An external peripheral is isolated as the trigger, or the failure persists independently.

steps.title: 6. Check Whether the Failure Is Function-Specific
steps.instructions: Determine whether the freeze or restart occurs only with a particular probe, accessory, workflow, export task, or imaging function. When safe, compare operation with known-good compatible accessories. Expected outcome: A repeatable external trigger is identified or accessory involvement is ruled out.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Normal Restart
steps.instructions: If the system is responsive enough to shut down normally, complete the standard shutdown and restart sequence. Avoid repeated hard power interruptions unless the system is completely nonresponsive and approved procedures permit them. Expected outcome: The system restarts normally and remains stable during basic operation.

steps.title: 8. Verify Basic Operation Under Observation
steps.instructions: Check startup, display and controls, probe recognition, basic imaging, and other normal functions relevant to the reported event. Observe for recurrence without unnecessarily prolonging testing on an unstable device. Expected outcome: The system remains stable through appropriate functional verification. If the external cause was corrected and no instability returns, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Remove From Service for Recurrent Instability
steps.instructions: If unexpected shutdowns, freezes, or restarts recur after external power, peripherals, accessories, and environmental factors have been ruled out, remove the system from service. Intermittent recovery does not establish reliability. Expected outcome: An unstable system is prevented from returning to patient care without further evaluation.

steps.title: 10. Escalate for Qualified Evaluation
steps.instructions: Provide the observed pattern, circumstances, messages, and reproduction information to qualified service personnel. Do not perform internal computer, storage, power-supply, cooling, or board-level repair without appropriate authorization. CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external AC power connection was loose and could be interrupted by normal movement of the system.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the power connection, verified stable startup and imaging operation without further interruption, and returned the unit to service.
